policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Algeria visa-free short visit
policies.summary: The current official MFA diplomatic-post schedule expressly sets an all-non-Algerian default and names these ordinary nationalities as its visa-exempt exceptions. This is a direct nationality schedule, not a conclusion from an online application channel or from an omitted country.
conditions: The schedule names nationals, while separately listing diplomatic and official-passport exemptions. This policy is therefore limited to ordinary passport nationality and does not extend special-document privileges to other passports.

No current official source in this batch states a nationality-wide exemption duration, ports, fee, onward-ticket, accommodation, health or extension rule. Admission, public-order and security decisions remain case-specific.

The Dublin MFA mission page omits Morocco, but two separate current MFA-post schedules (Oslo and London) expressly include it in the same closed ordinary-nationality list. Morocco is assigned on that corroborated direct evidence; the unexplained Dublin omission remains a source-quality risk.
The official Grand Sud organized-tourist arrival measure and the separate Algerian-national/foreign-passport document exception are conditional routes, not ordinary passport-nationality exemptions.

Work, residence, family, medical, study, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee and stateless-document routes are outside this ordinary short-visitor baseline. The law remains subject to international agreements and reciprocity.

policies.title: All other ordinary passports: Algeria advance consular visitor visa
policies.summary: The MFA schedule expressly answers that all non-Algerians require a visa except its closed named exemption list. Combined with the central MFA instruction to obtain that visa before travel from a diplomatic or consular post, this establishes the remaining ordinary-passport complement as visa_required, not evisa or visa_on_arrival.
conditions: This is the central MFA's advance diplomatic-or-consular process. Downloadable application forms are not electronic visa issuance, and no current official source reviewed here establishes an ordinary-passport visa-on-arrival or eVisa alternative for this cohort.

The central MFA guidance requires a passport valid at least six months, travel-assistance/repatriation insurance, photos and the purpose-specific documents; tourist applicants need legalized accommodation, hotel booking or a travel-agency attestation. The competent mission is normally the applicant's place of habitual residence.

The law sets a maximum consular-visa validity of two years and a maximum stay of 90 days per entry; actual type, duration, entries, fee, grant, extension and admission remain visa- and case-specific. It also requires sufficient means and permits refusal on public-order, State-security or fundamental-interest grounds.

The official Great South measure offers an arrival regularisation visa only to foreign tourist groups travelling through an organized tourism framework, with a stay no longer than 30 days. Its route, agency and case conditions do not establish nationality-wide visa-on-arrival access.

Do not apply this passport-nationality baseline to holders of diplomatic, official, service, crew, UN or other special documents, to residents or workers, to family and other purpose-specific visas, to transit or border regularisation, or to an Algerian national travelling with a foreign passport and separate Algerian biometric passport or identity document. Those are conditional/document cases, not an ordinary foreign-passport nationality route.

application.label: Algerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa guidance
application.processingTime: The central guidance gives a 48-hour issuance statement only for organized tourists after the complete file reaches the competent mission; it does not promise a general processing time.
steps: Download and complete the visa form in duplicate, then gather the passport, photographs, travel insurance and purpose-specific supporting documents.
Submit the application to the Algerian Embassy or Consulate responsible for the applicant's usual residence, with the required consular fee.
Obtain the visa before travel and present the travel document and visa for border examination; a visa does not remove admissibility and security controls.

policies.title: Algerian citizens: national-passport return
policies.summary: The Interior Ministry's current national-passport guidance directly states that the document permits its holder to leave Algeria or return to it under the applicable law. The same-country ordinary-passport pair is therefore citizenship, not a foreign visitor-visa classification.
conditions: This records only the citizen return function of an Algerian national passport. It does not decide passport issuance or validity, dual nationality, identity checks, customs, health, criminal process, security screening or other border formalities.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: Angola tourist-visa exemption
policies.summary: Presidential Decree 189/23 expressly lists 98 beneficiary countries. Ninety-six map to this repository’s passport catalog; Cook Islands and Niue have no separate codes in that catalog. A later official MIREX notice reports approval of an amendment for the Philippines, but no official Gazette promulgation or effective date was recovered, so it is not promoted here.
conditions: Tourist visits only.
Up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per calendar year.
Passport validity of more than six months and, where needed, an international vaccination certificate remain required.
This policy does not establish work, study, medical-treatment, residence, business-specific, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document or individual admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Antigua and Barbuda nationals: outside foreign visitor scope
policies.summary: The foreign-national visa routes do not establish a visitor-entry classification for an Antigua and Barbuda passport holder.
conditions: This does not determine the treatment of a dual national travelling on a foreign passport or any individual departure, document, security or admission requirement.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa-free visitors
policies.summary: The current Immigration Department list expressly names these ordinary-passport nationalities as not requiring a visa. China and Cuba have a distinct 30-day cap; other listed visitors are normally admitted for holiday or business for up to six months if the published conditions are met.
conditions: China and Cuba are exempt only where travel does not exceed 30 days. The live list's section heading calls its other named European group EU but also names Serbia; this policy follows the explicit country names, not the inaccurate regional label.

For other named nationals, holiday or business stays may not exceed six months and require a valid passport, onward/return ticket, accommodation confirmation and evidence of funds. Admission remains discretionary.
This does not establish work, residence, study, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: advance eVisa
policies.summary: The Immigration Department explicitly says countries not in its visa-exempt lists require a visa, and its eVisa Unit processes online applications for every person who requires one. The nationality complement is therefore normalized as evisa.
conditions: Apply electronically through the Immigration Department's entry-eVisa route. The eVisa is an official entry document, obtained after the Department decides the online application and paid electronically; it is not an ETA.

The eVisa FAQ says the route is for a travel-document holder requiring a visa and that a traveller who arrives without a visa is undocumented and may be refused entry. The baseline status is therefore not visa_on_arrival.

A separate, conditional 30-day tourist visa on arrival may be granted to a visitor who holds a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa or permanent-resident card, has no Antigua and Barbuda residence/occupation, travels solely for tourism/casual visits, and has a passport valid at least six months. This document-based exception does not change the nationality baseline.

The eVisa application requires a passport/travel document valid at least six months, photo, journey evidence, accommodation or sponsor evidence, funds and other requested documents. It is for tourism; work, residence, student, transit, cruise, diplomatic, official, special-document and admission cases remain separate.

A normally visa-required cruise visitor arriving in the morning and departing that evening, or a same-day in-transit passenger remaining in the airport's controlled space with onward proof, has a narrow special exception not represented by this ordinary visitor policy.

application.label: Antigua and Barbuda entry eVisa application
application.processingTime: The Immigration Department FAQ states a decision within seven working days, potentially extended to 15 days or, exceptionally, 30 days.
steps: Apply through the Immigration Department entry-eVisa route before travel.
Upload the required passport, photo, trip, accommodation/sponsor and financial evidence, then pay electronically.
Carry the approved eVisa and supporting travel documents to border control; the Department may still refuse admission.

policies.title: Argentine nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: DNM's tourist visa matrix applies to foreign passport nationalities, not Argentine nationals.
conditions: This classification does not establish the documents, carrier requirements, dual-national treatment, exit conditions, or admission decision for a particular Argentine national.
It does not resolve entry when a dual national presents a different country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: DNM-listed ordinary passports: tourist visa exemption
policies.summary: DNM's exhaustive ordinary-tourist passport matrix has no visa requirement in the ordinary-passport column for these nationalities.
conditions: This is limited to the DNM matrix's ordinary-passport tourist column. Blank ordinary-tourist cells are treated as the table's express visa-exempt entry rule; no complement is inferred.

A tourist enters for rest or recreation, is normally authorized for up to three months, may request one comparable extension, and may not perform remunerated work. Transit, frontier transit, crew, academic, medical, special, work, study, and residence are separate Migration Law categories.

Mercosur and associated-national rows remain ordinary visa-exempt entries, but DNM separately permits Brazil, Bolivia, Uruguay, Paraguay, Chile, Peru, Venezuela, Ecuador and Colombia to use specified valid national identity or travel documents. This passport policy does not extend that document option to other nationalities.

The ordinary-passport table separately shows diplomatic/service outcomes for some nationalities. This policy does not establish diplomatic, official, service, refugee, alien, emergency, laissez-passer, certificate-of-travel, residence, or other special-document treatment. Admission and any separate health, carrier, or border control requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: China, Dominican Republic and India: conditional ordinary tourist visa exemption
policies.summary: Current 2025 Argentine resolutions waive both a consular visa and AVE for these ordinary passports only when the traveller presents the specified valid United States visa and stays within the stated tourist/business scope.
conditions: China and Dominican Republic require an ordinary passport plus a valid, current United States visa of a similar migratory category. Dominican Republic is tourist-only, up to 90 days; China is tourist or the specified business category, up to 30 days.

India requires an ordinary passport plus a valid, current United States visa of a similar migratory category, verified as required; it is tourist-only and up to 90 days. Its rule took effect 28 August 2025.

These are conditional exemptions, not general visa-free status for the passport codes. A person outside the stated conditions must obtain a consular visa; no change of migratory category is allowed and a single comparable extension remains subject to DNM assessment.

DNM's AVE portal also mentions a United States green card for China, while Resolution 316/2025's operative text specifies a valid United States visa. The resolution is treated as controlling for this legal condition; the portal wording is preserved as an operational discrepancy for review.

policies.title: DNM-listed ordinary passports: AVE electronic travel authorization
policies.summary: The listed ordinary passport nationalities are eligible to seek Argentina's AVE electronic travel authorization instead of a consular tourist visa only when they meet DNM's additional United States document and history requirements.
conditions: AVE is an electronic travel authorization, not an eVisa or visa-on-arrival. It applies to valid ordinary passports travelling as tourists, only for nationalities in DNM's current AVE list.

An applicant must hold a valid United States B2, J, B1, O, P, E or H-1B visa covering the AVE processing, AVE validity and intended Argentine stay. A person from a United States visa-exempt jurisdiction may instead show a verified U.S. entry in the preceding two years, a valid ESTA, or one of the stated visas.

DNM says an AVE tourist authorization is valid for three months, permits a three-month tourist stay from first entry with multiple entries/exits, and may be extended once after DNM assessment. DNM has up to 20 working days to decide and may extend that period.

Taiwan's ordinary-tourist matrix row states 'visa / travel certificate'; AVE eligibility does not erase document-recognition or certificate requirements. The same caution applies to every diplomatic, official, service, special, refugee, alien, residence, work, study, crew, transit, or other non-ordinary-document case.
Approval is not guaranteed. Complete the fee step and online application through DNM; do not enter before the authorization is issued.

application.label: Argentina DNM AVE Global
application.processingTime: DNM states up to 20 working days for tourist AVE decisions, extendable when necessary.
steps: Confirm that the passport nationality is on DNM's current AVE list and that the additional United States eligibility evidence is valid.
Use DNM's AVE portal to pay the fee and submit the online application.
Wait for DNM's decision before travelling; an AVE is not an arrival-issued visa.

policies.title: DNM-listed ordinary passports: consular tourist visa required
policies.summary: DNM's exhaustive ordinary-tourist matrix expressly marks these nationalities 'REQUIERE VISA' or a visa/travel-certificate requirement. Any separate AVE or 2025 conditional United States-visa exception is retained as a narrow overlapping route, not silently converted into general visa-free access.
conditions: This policy consists only of DNM's explicit ordinary-tourist rows marked 'REQUIERE VISA' (and Kosovo/Taiwan's 'visa / travel certificate' rows). It is not a nationality complement inferred outside the official matrix.

China, India and the Dominican Republic have the separate conditional United States-visa tourist exemptions in the other policy; all three still display as visa-required in the matrix for travellers without that exception. The AVE-eligible countries likewise remain visa-required if the AVE conditions or authorization are absent.

For the consular tourist visa route, Argentina's official service guidance requires a passport valid for at least six months, a completed application, financial proof, return reservation, accommodation/itinerary or invitation, fee and consular interview. Apply through the Argentine consular representation with jurisdiction.

The tourist category is for rest/recreation, normally up to three months and renewable once; it does not permit remunerated work. Transit, crew, work, study, residence, diplomatic/official/service, refugee, special travel certificate and other Migration Law categories are separate and cannot be inferred from this ordinary-passport policy.

application.label: Argentina tourist visa guidance
steps: Confirm the ordinary-passport rule and whether a separate AVE or statutory conditional exemption applies.
Contact the competent Argentine consular representation to arrange the required tourist-visa interview.
Submit the official travel, financial, passport, itinerary/accommodation and other consular documents before travel.

policies.title: Armenian citizenship
policies.summary: An Armenian ordinary passport belongs to an Armenian citizen and is outside the foreign visitor-visa schedule.
conditions: Does not decide dual-national document choice, residence, work, exit, transit, security, or individual border treatment.

policies.title: Ordinary passports returned as visa-free by the live MFA checker
policies.summary: For an ordinary PASSPORT and tourism/relatives purpose, the current MFA E-Visa eligibility endpoint returns ALLOW_WITHOUT_VISA for these passports.
conditions: The checked route is ordinary PASSPORT (document type 167) and visitor purpose TOURISM_RELATIVES; it does not decide non-ordinary documents, work, residence, transit, or admission discretion.
The separate residence-permit programme is not this nationality-only result: it requires the stated six-month-valid qualifying permit and is active from 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027.

policies.title: Ordinary passports returned as eVisa-eligible by the live MFA checker
policies.summary: For an ordinary PASSPORT and tourism/relatives purpose, the current MFA E-Visa eligibility endpoint returns ALLOWED_FOR_EVISA for these non-exempt, non-invitation-listed passports.
conditions: The live response is an advance electronic-visa route for ordinary PASSPORT and TOURISM_RELATIVES; it is not an arrival-visa classification even where a separate API field mentions border processing.

The temporary residence-permit exemption is conditional on a qualifying physical/sticker permit with at least six months' validity and ends 1 July 2027; it does not replace the passport-only baseline.

policies.title: Ordinary passports returned as consulate-only
policies.summary: The current MFA E-Visa eligibility endpoint returns ONLY_CONSULATE for these ordinary-passport tourism/relatives queries.
conditions: Sudan and Togo also appear on the MFA's published invitation-only list. Kosovo is consulate-only in the live checker but is not named on that list.
This is not a classification for diplomatic, official, service, refugee, alien, transit, residence, work, or case-specific documents and purposes.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: no advance Bahamas visitor visa
policies.summary: The Bahamas MOFA currently lists these named nationalities and territories as not needing a visa to enter The Bahamas.
conditions: This policy maps only unambiguous current-country entries from MOFA’s list. It does not map the list’s separate territorial or historic labels to another passport code.

For HK, this represents only the page’s named Hong Kong entry; it does not establish treatment for a PRC passport, Hong Kong Certificate of Identity, British National (Overseas), residence document, or another special document.
The page does not give a visa-free visit period for this list. It does not establish employment, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, or special-document access.
Admission remains subject to border inspection. The Immigration Act permits an immigration officer to require a passport, visa, nationality/identity document, or permission-to-enter document.
The separate Indian third-country visa or residence exception is deliberately modelled in its own conditional policy.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Bahamas Electronic Entry Visa visitor route
policies.summary: The listed nationalities require a Bahamas visa; MOFA provides the official Electronic Entry Visa application route for ordinary visitor visas, subject to its stated conditions.
conditions: The MOFA list expressly identifies these nationalities as needing a visa. India is included only for Indian nationals outside the separately stated third-country visa or permanent-residence exception.
An Electronic Entry Visa is not a guarantee of entry. Visa applicants need a passport with more than six months remaining, and the border officer may deny entry.
Visa-required travellers also need a visa when arriving by cruise ship from the United States. The policy does not establish a transit or cruise exception.
This ordinary visitor route is for leisure (self-sponsored or sponsored). Seaman’s visas are a distinct crew/trade route, and official and diplomatic visas are not available for online application.
Single-entry validity is three months. Multiple-entry visas have separate eligibility and stated three-month, six-month, or one-year periods; the page says three-year visas are not available online.

The ordinary visitor must apply through the official portal, complete the application, provide the stated supporting documents, pay if requested, and present the passport used to apply plus the Electronic Entry Visa on arrival.

application.label: Bahamas Electronic Entry Visa application
application.processingTime: 7–10 business days when supporting documents are in order and no interview is required.
steps: Select the visitor-visa type and submit the online application with passport, photograph, and country-specific supporting documents.
Pay the requested fee and attend an interview or provide additional documents if directed by the Visa Office.
Present the passport used for the application and the approved Electronic Entry Visa to Immigration on arrival.

policies.title: India ordinary passport: third-country visa or permanent-residence exception
policies.summary: An Indian national with a valid Schengen, UK, Canadian, or US visa, or permanent residence in one of those jurisdictions, does not need a Bahamas visa when presenting the stated evidence.
conditions: The traveller must present the qualifying valid third-country visa with the valid passport, or proof of qualifying permanent-resident status with the valid passport, to Bahamas Immigration.
All other Indian nationals require a Bahamas visa and are within the separate Electronic Entry Visa policy.
The page separately exempts Indian diplomatic and official passports; that non-ordinary document exception is not classified here.
This exception does not establish work, residence, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, or unconditional visa-free access, and entry remains subject to border inspection.

policies.title: Bahrain: GCC citizens do not need an entry visa
policies.summary: The Bahrain National Portal expressly exempts citizens of Kuwait, Oman, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Qatar from Bahrain’s entry-visa requirement.
conditions: Applies to citizenship of the five named GCC states, not merely residence in a GCC state.
The National Portal says other nationalities require an entry visa; this is not a visa-on-arrival, ETA, or eVisa.
NPRA separately offers electronic visas to GCC residents who meet its status and document conditions; that route does not alter the named GCC citizen exemption.
Same-flight or same-airport transit is separately visa-free under the Bahrain AIP and is outside this ordinary visitor classification.
Does not classify work, residence, family sponsorship, transit requiring entry, crew, diplomatic, official, service, UN, emergency, refugee, or other special-document entry.

policies.title: Bahrain: citizenship treatment
policies.summary: A Bahraini ordinary passport belongs to a Bahraini citizen and is not a foreign visitor-visa case.
conditions: Applies to Bahraini citizens holding a Bahraini ordinary passport.
Does not decide foreign residence, dual-national document choice, or foreign visitor treatment.

policies.title: Bangladesh: citizen right of re-entry
policies.summary: Bangladesh’s Constitution directly gives every citizen a qualified right to leave and re-enter Bangladesh.
conditions: Article 36 is subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the public interest. This is a citizen/right-of-entry normalization, not a foreign visitor visa or an exemption for a foreign passport held by a Bangladeshi-origin person.
The cited provision does not establish work, residence, transit, dual-nationality/document, admissibility, or departure-document rules.

policies.title: Bangladesh: named ordinary-passport visitor visa on arrival
policies.summary: Current Bangladesh MFA guidance expressly identifies this named nationality cohort as eligible to seek a visitor visa on arrival for official duty, business, investment or tourism, subject to document verification and officer satisfaction.
conditions: This is a conditional visa-on-arrival route, not visa-free entry. The expressly stated purposes are official duty, business, investment and tourism; for short tourism the guidance calls for hotel booking or personal invitation and a return ticket.

The same guidance limits its separate defence and security-force route to travellers with prior Ministry of Home Affairs clearance; that purpose-specific condition does not broaden ordinary tourist access.
The immigration officer at an airport or land port must examine the documents and be satisfied. The guidance states a maximum 30-day, single-entry visa; extension is only under existing visa policy.

Published checklist conditions include a valid passport, USD 500 (cash or card) except government duty, return ticket, supporting documents, and cash payment in USD/GBP/EUR. The stated USD 50 fee is subject to reciprocity/exempt-fee arrangements.
The portal’s online form must be printed and taken with supporting documents to a visa office or mission; it is not evidence of an electronically issued visa and is not normalized as eVisa or ETA.

NVR, Bangladeshi-origin, spouse/child, investor recommendation, UN/mission staff, diplomatic/official/service, seaman/UN travel document, residence, transit and third-country/no-mission pathways are document-, origin-, purpose-, route- or residence-conditioned and are deliberately excluded from this nationality-only policy.

policies.title: MOFA-listed ordinary passports: no Barbados entry visa
policies.summary: The current Barbados foreign-ministry table marks these named foreign nationalities as not requiring a visa to enter Barbados.
conditions: This policy maps only clear current-country rows from the Ministry table. The table’s China entry includes Macau and Hong Kong; CN, HK, and MO are limited to that stated combined entry and do not establish other PRC, Hong Kong, or Macao travel documents.

The table gives different maximum stays by nationality or agreement. No common duration is inferred; the traveller must meet the applicable named-row terms and any current Immigration admission requirements.
This does not establish a route for work, residence, study, crew, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, laissez-passer, territory-specific, or other special documents.

All visitors need the online Immigration and Customs Form available 72 hours before arrival, a passport valid for the trip, a return ticket, intended address, and evidence of personal support. Admission remains for the Immigration Officer.

policies.title: MOFA-listed ordinary passports: advance Barbados entry visa
policies.summary: The listed nationalities require an advance Barbados entry visa. The application is online, but Immigration describes the issued authorization as a letter, so this is not classified as a true eVisa.
conditions: The Ministry’s current foreign-national table marks these nationalities as visa required. The applicant must be granted permission before booking and confirming travel.

Immigration states that the issued visa is a letter accepted at airline check-in and by Barbados Immigration; the fully online application and payment process therefore do not establish an eVisa status.
An entry visa is a prerequisite to seek entry, not a guarantee of admission. Permission to enter is granted only by the Immigration Officer at the port of entry.

The standard single-entry authority is one entry within three months and the stated multiple-entry authority is within six months; application evidence, processing, and endorsements remain subject to the authority’s requirements.

Cruise passengers and crew have limited stated airport-to-vessel, same-vessel, and 12-hour transit exceptions. An overnighting crew member requires a visa, and diplomatic-corp fee treatment does not waive the application.

application.label: Barbados online entry-visa application
application.processingTime: Three weeks under Immigration’s published standard process.
steps: Create an account and complete the online entry-visa application and payment process before travel.
Provide the signed application, photograph, passport biographic-page copy, purpose and support documents, and residence-status evidence where applicable.
Carry the authorization letter and meet the visitor and border-inspection requirements on arrival.

policies.title: Haiti ordinary passport: advance Barbados entry visa unless document exception applies
policies.summary: A regular Haitian passport holder requires an advance Barbados entry visa unless the holder has the stated qualifying permanent-residence or Green Card document.
conditions: The Ministry table says a visa is required for regular Haitian passport holders and directs them to the Immigration online application portal.
The separate qualifying-resident exception and diplomatic/official passport treatment are not part of this standard ordinary-passport policy.
The authorization is an advance entry-visa letter rather than a true eVisa, and it does not guarantee entry. Visitor admission, purpose, transit, crew, and port-inspection rules remain applicable.

application.label: Barbados online entry-visa application
application.processingTime: Three weeks under Immigration’s published standard process.
steps: Submit the online entry-visa application and payment before travel.
Provide the required regular-passport and supporting documents.
Carry the issued authorization letter for airline check-in and Barbados Immigration.

policies.title: Haiti ordinary passport: qualifying permanent-resident or Green Card exception
policies.summary: A Haitian regular passport holder who is a permanent resident of the UK, United States, Canada, or Schengen countries, or holds a Green Card, does not require a Barbados visa under the Ministry’s stated exception.
conditions: This exception requires the stated qualifying residence or Green Card document; it is not unconditional Haitian ordinary-passport visa-free access.
The Ministry separately identifies diplomatic and official Haitian passports as visa-free; that special-document treatment is outside this ordinary-passport classification.
The visitor must still satisfy the published online form, passport, return-ticket, address, support, purpose, transit, and admission conditions.

policies.title: Belize: table entries marked visa required
policies.summary: The current Belize Immigration table directly marks these foreign ordinary-passport nationalities YES for a Belize entry visa. The application route is mission/Belmopan processing, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: A Belize entry visa normally authorizes up to 30 days from entry; longer visits require the stated visa and visitor-permit extension process.

This excludes the 30-day US/Schengen/Canadian multiple-entry visa or permanent-residence-card waiver, residence, work, study, transit, diplomatic, official, special-document, sponsor and individual-admission routes.
Passport validity is more than six months and a return itinerary is required by the published requirements.

policies.title: Belize: table entries marked visa not required
policies.summary: The current Belize Immigration table directly marks these foreign ordinary-passport nationalities NO for an entry visa.
conditions: The central page introduces the nationality exemption for visits not exceeding 30 days; listed longer-stay thresholds must be observed where shown.
Slovakia, Slovenia, South Sudan and Timor-Leste are not assigned here because the live named table contains no row for them; no residual exemption is inferred from omission.
This excludes residence, work, study, transit, diplomatic, official, special-document, sponsor, citizenship and individual-admission routes.
Passport validity, onward itinerary and border admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Benin: current named ordinary-passport visa waivers
policies.summary: The current Foreign Ministry agreement register expressly identifies these ordinary- or national-passport waiver entries, including the current UEMOA/ECOWAS free-movement entries.
conditions: The current Foreign Ministry register, not the 2020 general flyer, is the operative support for this named ordinary-passport cohort. It records both the country and the passport types covered by each agreement.
The reciprocal entries cover HT, HK, SG, BZ, DM, GD, MH, FM, AG, BS, BB, MY, PH and VC; its stated periods are 14 days for HK, 14 days for SG, 30 days for MY and PH, and three months for the others.

The UEMOA/ECOWAS entries cover SL, BF, CI, GW, ML, NE, SN, TG, CV, GM, NG, LR, GH and GN. The register identifies the applicable ECOWAS Protocol or UEMOA Treaty; duration and any travel-document conditions must be confirmed with the competent authorities.

The African-agreement entries cover ZA, TN, RW, CF, TD, CG, MU, ST, SC, KE and BI. Their register entries expressly include a national or ordinary passport and generally state three months, except ZA states one month.

The September 2020 MAEC flyer claiming a unilateral 53-African-country waiver is retained as historical official evidence but is not promoted for its other 28 codes. The current register lists several of those countries only for diplomatic/service passports and does not reproduce a 53-country unilateral rule.

This policy does not establish employment, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic/official, special-document, health, document-validity, prior-history, public-order, national-security or case-specific admissibility treatment. The separate 72-hour cruise exemption requires an approved travel agency.

policies.title: Benin: Beninese ordinary passport
policies.summary: A Beninese ordinary passport is issued to persons of Beninese nationality; this is not foreign visitor admission.
conditions: Applies to Beninese citizens holding an ordinary Beninese passport.
Does not decide dual-nationality document choice, foreign residence, or foreign-passport entry conditions.

policies.title: Bermuda: full British-citizen passports visa-free for a short visit
policies.summary: Current UK government Bermuda guidance states that a holder of a full British citizen passport travelling from the UK may visit without a visa for up to 180 days in any 12-month period. This is visa-free, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The UK source expressly limits this statement to people travelling on a full British citizen passport from the UK; it does not establish treatment for other British-national statuses or special British documents.
The stated limit is up to 180 days in any 12-month period and requires a return or onward ticket.
Work, study, business, residence, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, special-document, territory-belonger and individual-admission arrangements are excluded.

policies.title: Bhutan: Indian ordinary passports with entry permit at the port of entry
policies.summary: Bhutan's Department of Immigration expressly makes Indian nationals eligible for an entry permit at the port of entry. This arrival-issued authorization is normalized as visa on arrival, not visa-free admission.
conditions: This is an entry permit issued at the port of entry, not a visa-free finding. The portal says an original passport or Voter Identity Card is required; the latter document route is outside this ordinary-passport policy.
The official tourism page says the permit may instead be applied for before travel, including through a tour operator or hotel; online processing alone is not classified as eVisa.

Tourist stay is stated as a maximum of 90 days. The portal states an Indian visitor SDF of INR 1,200 per night; special child, day-visitor, border-town, extension, admissibility and other-purpose rules remain applicable.
Does not decide work, residence, study, transit, crew, border-pass, diplomatic, official, service, special-document or case-specific admission rules.

policies.title: Bhutan: Bangladeshi and Maldivian ordinary passports with visa on arrival
policies.summary: The Department of Immigration expressly names Bangladesh and the Maldives as eligible for visas on arrival.
conditions: The Tourism authority says these visitors require a visa, but use the Indian permit-process workflow; that workflow does not convert their express arrival-issued visa into visa-free admission.

Tourist stay is stated as a maximum of 90 days. A Sustainable Development Fee applies; the tourism authority states USD 100 per adult per day, while the immigration FAQ describes the underlying USD 200 rate and its USD 100 incentive through 31 August 2027.
The authority retains admission discretion at the port of entry. Passport validity, fee, SDF, extension, funds, tour, health, security and individual-admissibility requirements remain applicable.
Does not decide SAARC Visa Exemption Sticker holders, or diplomatic, official, service, residence, work, study, transit, crew, special-document or case-specific rules.

policies.title: Bhutan: all other foreign ordinary passports requiring eVisa before entry
policies.summary: The Department of Immigration's exhaustive entry page says all other foreign nationals must obtain an eVisa before entering Bhutan. The eVisa classification rests on that explicit term, not merely on the availability of an online application.
conditions: The official portal says applications must be submitted at least 15 days before intended arrival; the tourism authority describes review within five working days after submission, so travellers should follow the stricter stated lead time.

Tourist stay is stated as a maximum of 90 days. The visa application fee is USD 40 and the current tourism page states a USD 100-per-day adult SDF; the portal describes a USD 200 base rate with a USD 100 incentive through 31 August 2027.
A valid SAARC Visa Exemption Sticker is a special-document exception to prior eVisa/entry-permit clearance; it is not an ordinary-passport nationality-wide exemption.
Thailand and Switzerland visa-on-arrival treatment on the entry page is expressly limited to diplomatic or official passports, not these ordinary-passport policies.
Does not decide residence, work, study, transit, crew, border-pass, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, security, health, refusal or other case-specific rules.

application.label: Bhutan Immigration Services Portal
application.processingTime: The tourism authority says submitted applications are reviewed within five working days; the immigration portal says to apply at least 15 days before arrival.
steps: Create an account in the Bhutan Immigration Services Portal.
Provide passport copy, photograph, travel details and payment information.
Submit the visa application and pay the visa fee and Sustainable Development Fee.
Obtain the Department of Immigration eVisa clearance before travel.

policies.title: Bhutan: Bhutanese citizenship entry
policies.summary: The Home Affairs notice directly regulates Bhutanese citizens entering Bhutan with a passport or citizenship identity card, supporting the citizenship classification for the same-country pair.
conditions: At land ports, Bhutanese entering or exiting must produce a passport or Citizenship Identity Card and complete immigration formalities.
This citizenship classification does not decide foreign ordinary-passport visas, residence, dual-nationality, refugee, special-document, route, security or individual-admissibility issues.

policies.title: Bolivia: eight named ordinary passports added to Group I
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry expressly says these eight nationalities entered Group I without a visa requirement. This is visa-free tourism/visitor access, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The official announcement directly names this closed eight-nationality cohort as entering Group I without a visa requirement.
It does not establish a visa status for any unlisted nationality; no complement is inferred.

The source does not specify stay duration, entries, fee, extension, admission outcome, health, funds or onward-travel conditions. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Bolivia: Honduran ordinary passports visa-free for tourism or visit
policies.summary: Bolivia’s Foreign Ministry states that Honduran and Bolivian citizens may travel between the two countries without a tourist or visit visa from 17 March 2024. This is visa-free access, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The Ministry expressly makes the mutual tourist-or-visit visa suppression effective for Honduran citizens entering Bolivia.
The announcement refers to diplomatic, official and ordinary passports; this policy records only the ordinary-passport tourism/visit route.
No duration, entries, fee, extension, admission outcome, health, funds or onward-travel condition is inferred.

policies.title: Bolivia: Dominican ordinary passports visa-free for tourism
policies.summary: Bolivia’s Foreign Ministry states that Dominican citizens could enter Bolivia without processing a tourism visa from 2 September 2024. This is visa-free access, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The Ministry expressly identifies Dominican citizens entering Bolivia without a tourism visa and identifies ordinary passports in the underlying agreement.

No duration, entries, fee, extension, admission outcome, health, funds or onward-travel condition is inferred. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Bolivia: Brazilian ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: The officially promulgated Bolivia–Brazil agreement directly permits nationals of either party to enter the other without a visa and expressly preserves use of an international passport. This is visa-free access, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: This policy follows the agreement’s direct no-visa entry rule for Brazilian nationals travelling to Bolivia; it is not inferred from Mercosur membership or from a document alternative.
The agreement permits the use of an international passport even though it also provides a national-identity-document route.

It states a stay of up to 90 days, extendable for another 90 days in a year, for official, tourism or business activities. Other purpose and admission conditions remain outside this ordinary short-visitor baseline.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa-free short visitors
policies.summary: The official Washington Embassy's full current named visa-free schedule supports this reconcilable ordinary-passport cohort. Passports disputed by the current statutory Tourism Organisation schedule are excluded.
conditions: The Embassy lists this cohort among countries whose citizens do not require a visa. It does not establish visa-free work, residence, business, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special-document or individual-admissibility treatment.

Government guidance requires a passport valid at least six months in the absence of a specific bilateral agreement, caps visitor stays at 90 days in each calendar year, and says extensions are available from Immigration.
No general arrival authorization or visa-on-arrival status is inferred. Border officials may apply normal documentary, health, security and admission controls.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: advance online tourist visa
policies.summary: The official Washington Embassy required-country schedule, supplemented for Marshall Islands by the statutory Tourism Organisation's required list, establishes a visitor visa requirement. The Department of Immigration makes the tourist application available online through the official eVisa portal and at missions; it is normalized as an advance eVisa route.
conditions: Submit the tourism-visa application before travel through the official eVisa portal, or at an Immigration office, Botswana mission or consulate. The Department says online approval/rejection is accessed in the portal.

An online-approved traveller may travel with the approval letter as proof of the visa; Immigration prints the visa at the airport or other port of entry. This post-approval printing is not a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival finding.

The Government page says the service takes 7–14 working days. A tourism visa is for recreational travel, with a single entry up to one month or multiple entry up to three months; it does not authorize work, residence, business-only, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.

The application requires a passport valid at least six months, photographs, covering letter, flight and accommodation itinerary, trip itinerary and intention to depart; a re-entry permit may be required for the country of residence. Approval and admission remain discretionary.

Government visitor information caps visitors at 90 days in each calendar year and permits extensions through Immigration. The cited nationality schedules lack effective dates and include obsolete or inconsistent country labels; the eVisa frontend is dated 2021 and did not yield selector evidence. Reconfirm directly with Immigration before travel or promotion.

application.label: Botswana Government eVisa service
application.processingTime: Government tourism-visa guidance states 7–14 working days after application.
steps: Apply online through the official Botswana eVisa service before travel, or submit Form 1 at Immigration or a Botswana mission or consulate.
Upload the stated passport, photographs, purpose, itinerary, accommodation and onward-departure evidence; supply any required residence-country re-entry documentation.
Wait for approval before travel, carry the approval letter and supporting documents, and complete Immigration examination and visa printing at the port of entry.

policies.title: Brazilian nationals: outside the foreign VIVIS regime
policies.summary: The QGRV governs entry of foreigners; a Brazilian national is therefore outside its foreign visitor-visa classification.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish the document requirements for a particular Brazilian national, dual national, carrier, or border route.
It does not determine treatment when a dual national presents a different country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: QGRV-listed ordinary passports: VIVIS visa exemption
policies.summary: For these ordinary national passports, the QGRV VIVIS column records a visa dispensation for a short visitor stay. China is handled by the later country-specific MRE update.
conditions: The QGRV legend limits this policy to the VIVIS column for holders of ordinary passports. PADIP (diplomatic) and PASOF (official or service) columns are separate and are not normalized here.

The precise dispensation period is the numbered VIVIS entry and applicable footnote in the QGRV, rather than a single uniform duration; the table uses 30-, 60-, 90-, 180-, and other specified periods.
A QGRV # marker permits entry with a civil identity card for the marked nationality. This passport classification neither requires nor generalizes that separate identity-card facility.
This policy does not cover a laissez-passer, refugee or alien travel document, diplomatic, official, service, public-affairs, temporary, or other special passport/document.

Visa dispensation is not a residence authorization and does not authorize paid work. VIVIS is limited to visitor purposes; a different purpose, a longer stay, or residence requires the applicable immigration route.

Admission and the authorized stay remain subject to Brazilian border control and all current entry requirements. Any extension is a separate Polícia Federal process and depends on the applicable QGRV reciprocity rule.

policies.title: China ordinary passports: VIVIS visa exemption
policies.summary: MRE's current Zurich consular guidance says Chinese ordinary passport holders have been exempt from VIVIS since 11 May 2026 for the specified short-visit purposes.
conditions: The MRE guidance limits the exemption to multiple-entry tourism, business, transit, artistic, or sports visits, for at most 30 days in one year.
Longer stays and other purposes require the appropriate physical visa under the MRE guidance.

This applies to an ordinary Chinese passport; it does not establish treatment of a PRC Travel Document, Hong Kong SAR passport, Macao SAR passport, Taiwan passport, diplomatic passport, official passport, or another special document.
The consular page's country-specific online filing note does not establish a nationality-wide eVisa category for this normalized visitor classification.

policies.title: Australia, Canada, and United States ordinary passports: electronic VIVIS
policies.summary: Australia, Canada, and United States nationals require a Brazilian visitor visa from 10 April 2025 but may obtain the nationally described electronic visitor visa.
conditions: The MRE source describes this as a visitor visa (VIVIS), not visa-free entry; it is valid only for the visitor purposes and periods the visa grants.
The electronic route is expressly described by MRE for these three nationalities. Generic online consular processing for other nationalities is not normalized as eVisa.
This policy is limited to ordinary national passports and does not establish a rule for diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, alien, or other special travel documents.
A visitor visa does not establish residence or permission for paid employment; entry and admission remain subject to Brazilian immigration control.

application.label: Brazil electronic visitor visa application
steps: Use the MRE-linked electronic visitor-visa application site.
Complete the visitor-visa application and provide the requested supporting documents.
Receive the electronic visa before travel and present it with the ordinary passport used for the application.

policies.title: QGRV-listed ordinary passports: VIVIS required
policies.summary: For these ordinary national passports, the QGRV VIVIS column records that a Brazilian visitor visa is required before the short visit.
conditions: This is limited to the QGRV VIVIS column for an ordinary passport. It does not infer a rule from PADIP, PASOF, residence status, special passport, laissez-passer, refugee document, or alien travel document.
The required visa is a visitor visa; purpose, length, and entry conditions are assessed under the visa and ordinary migration rules, and the visa does not itself authorize residence or paid work.
For Haitian nationals, the later MRE notice says QGRV was updated to require prior consultation with MRE Brasília for VIVIS. That additional case-management condition remains applicable.
For Taiwan, the QGRV's distinct treatment is document-specific; this ISO-code policy does not establish admission on a Taiwan diplomatic, official, or special passport.

policies.title: Brunei: Category D1 ordinary-passport 90-day visa waiver
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns these ordinary passports to Category D1, whose conditions expressly waive a visa for up to 90 days.
conditions: The D1 waiver is up to 90 days. A visa application is required for a longer stay and for business visits; no work, residence, professional visit or extension right is established.

E-Arrival Card registration supplies arrival/travel/accommodation information and a reference number. Immigration separately requires a visa if applicable, so the declaration is not normalized as an ETA or visa authorization.
A recognised passport with at least six months’ validity is required. Admission, funds, onward travel, security, health and immigration-officer conditions remain separate.

policies.title: Brunei: Category D2 ordinary-passport 30-day visa waiver
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns these ordinary passports to Category D2, whose conditions expressly waive a visa for up to 30 days.
conditions: The D2 waiver is up to 30 days. A visa application is required for a longer stay and for business visits; no work, residence, professional visit or extension right is established.

The statutory Schedule 2 exemption is limited to entry by air through Brunei International Airport and requires the Controller to be satisfied of confirmed return or outward passage. This policy preserves that route and onward-travel condition.
E-Arrival Card registration is an arrival declaration, not an ETA or visa authorization; the Immigration guidance separately calls for a visa when applicable.

A recognised passport with at least six months’ validity, ordinary admission rules and individual officer assessment apply. Diplomatic, official, service and special-document arrangements are excluded.

policies.title: Brunei: Category D3 ordinary-passport 14-day visa waiver
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns these ordinary passports to Category D3, whose conditions expressly waive a visa for up to 14 days.
conditions: The D3 waiver is up to 14 days. A visa application is required for a longer stay and for business visits; no work, residence, professional visit or extension right is established.

The statutory Schedule 3 exemption remains subject to conditions the Controller of Immigration may impose. Kosovo is expressly added to that schedule by the 2026 Gazette amendment, and the current MFA schedule places its ordinary passport in D3.
E-Arrival Card registration is a declaration, not an ETA or visa authorization. A recognised passport with at least six months’ validity and individual admissibility conditions apply.

policies.title: Brunei: Category C1 ordinary-passport 30-day visa on arrival
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns these ordinary passports to Category C1, whose conditions permit a visa-on-arrival application for 30 days.
conditions: C1 permits an application for single- or multiple-entry visa on arrival for 30 days, with the published BND20/BND30 fees and visa form/arrival-card procedure.

A visa application is required for a longer stay and for business visits; the arrival route does not establish work, residence, professional-visit, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document access.
E-Arrival Card registration is a declaration, not an ETA and not the visa-on-arrival itself. Passport validity, admission and all individual requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Brunei: Category C2 Saudi ordinary-passport 14-day visa on arrival
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns Saudi ordinary passports to Category C2, which permits a single-entry 14-day visa-on-arrival application.
conditions: C2 permits a single-entry 14-day visa-on-arrival application, with the published BND20 fee and visa form/arrival-card procedure.
A visa application is required for a longer stay and for business visits; no work, residence, professional visit, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document access is established.
E-Arrival Card registration is a declaration, not an ETA or visa authorization. Passport validity, admission and individual conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Brunei: Category C3 Qatar ordinary-passport 14-day visa on arrival
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns Qatari ordinary passports to Category C3, whose conditions permit a 14-day visa-on-arrival application.
conditions: C3 permits an application for single- or multiple-entry visa on arrival for 14 days, with the published BND20 fee and visa form/arrival-card procedure.
A visa application is required for a longer stay and for business visits; no work, residence, professional visit, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document access is established.
E-Arrival Card registration is a declaration, not an ETA or visa authorization. Passport validity, admission and individual conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Brunei: Category C4 Bahrain ordinary-passport 14-day visa on arrival
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns Bahraini ordinary passports to Category C4, whose conditions permit a 14-day visa-on-arrival application.
conditions: C4 permits an application for single- or multiple-entry visa on arrival for 14 days, with the published BND20/BND30 fees and visa form/arrival-card procedure.
A visa application is required for a longer stay and for business visits; no work, residence, professional visit, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document access is established.
E-Arrival Card registration is a declaration, not an ETA or visa authorization. Passport validity, admission and individual conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Brunei: Category A and B ordinary passports require advance visa
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns these ordinary passports to Categories A or B; both categories expressly require a visa through a Brunei mission abroad.
conditions: The assignment comes from the explicit, live MFA country-by-country Category A/B schedule—not from an unlisted-country complement. Both categories say a visa is required and may be applied for through the nearest Brunei mission abroad; the reviewed material does not establish an electronic alternative.

The FAQ distinguishes short/social, business and professional visit visas. Business and professional visits require a Brunei registered/government-linked sponsor application, and employment needs the appropriate visa and employment pass before arrival.

E-Arrival Card registration is an arrival declaration and does not replace the required visa. Transit is separately limited to a 72-hour transit pass with onward ticket and airline sponsor/guarantor; it is not normalized as a visitor route.

Valid recognised passport, six-month validity, fees, duration, entry count, documentary criteria and individual admissibility remain subject to the competent authorities. Diplomatic, official, service, residence and special-document arrangements are excluded.

policies.title: African ordinary passports: Burkina Faso electronic short-entry visa with fee waiver
policies.summary: The Council of Ministers’ current Africa-wide fee-waiver decision expressly says the waiver is not a visa exemption. The official Embassy guidance requires online entry-visa applications and emails an eVisa for presentation at the border. This maps the catalog’s foreign ordinary passports of African states to the advance electronic short-visitor route.
conditions: The 11 September 2025 decision removes visa fees for nationals of African countries but expressly retains the visa requirement. It does not provide a visa-free ordinary-passport cohort, a duration, or a statutory exemption from normal immigration, health, security and admissibility checks.

The Embassy says that, since 1 February 2023, entry-visa applications are online; after approval, the applicant receives an email attachment labelled “EVISA” and presents it on arrival. It describes transit visas (1–5 days) and short-stay visas (1–90 days); tourism is within the short-stay visitor purpose and business, work, residence and long stay are not normalized here.

The official portal and embassy distinguish ordinary-passport electronic applications from diplomatic, service and UN laissez-passer applications. The latter, refugee, alien, emergency and other special travel documents are outside this policy.

A live National Police page says land-border and Ouagadougou-airport short visas may be issued to foreign travellers. Its stated fee is incompatible with the 2025 nationwide African fee waiver and with the newer Visa Burkina fee schedule. That page has no publication or update date and conflicts with the Embassy’s online-only wording, so it is retained as a material operational conflict rather than used to normalize an all-nationality visa_on_arrival route.

ECOWAS’s 2025 transitional statement continues visa-free movement for Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger citizens in ECOWAS states until further notice. It does not publish a reciprocal inbound ordinary-passport exemption at Burkina Faso after its withdrawal; the newer Burkina Faso Government decision controls the African visitor cohort modeled here.

A valid passport, short-visit supporting documents, a return/onward arrangement, vaccination or health documents, entry-port controls, individual decision/refusal and security checks may be required. Approval is not a guarantee of admission.

application.label: Visa Burkina electronic entry-visa service
application.processingTime: The Embassy says a successful applicant receives the eVisa email attachment after the request is accepted; no reliable current uniform processing time was published.
steps: Open the official Visa Burkina platform and register/select the appropriate transit or short-stay entry-visa route.
Submit the online application, passport and purpose/health documents, then complete any applicable online payment step; African nationals have a current visa-fee waiver.
If approved, receive the emailed EVISA document and present it with the passport at an official land or international-airport entry point.

policies.title: Foreign EAC ordinary passports: Burundi visa-free short-visitor entry
policies.summary: Current EAC sources identify the seven other Partner States and state that all Partner States implement visa-free entry for Partner-State citizens. This maps the seven foreign EAC passport codes to Burundi visa-free entry. Burundi Tourism separately says all foreigners need a visa except EAC citizens, but its parenthetical list omits Somalia; the current EAC sources control that new Partner-State mapping.
conditions: Applies only to citizens holding ordinary passports of the seven other current EAC Partner States: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda.

The EAC free-movement guarantee remains subject to host-State public-policy, public-security, public-health, border-document and individual-admissibility controls; it is not a work, residence, refugee, diplomatic, official, service, crew or special-document classification.

CGM describes a free EAC access visa issued for up to six months and says it does not grant a right to work. This post-entry administrative status does not turn the entry rule into a visa-on-arrival requirement.

Burundi Tourism’s current page calls EAC the exception but names only Kenya, Uganda, DRC, Rwanda, Tanzania and South Sudan. Somalia is retained under the current EAC Partner-State and all-Partner-State implementation evidence; this source discrepancy should be rechecked.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Burundi simple entry visa at Melchior Ndadaye International Airport
policies.summary: Burundi Tourism’s current visitor guidance expressly requires a visa for every foreigner other than EAC citizens. The directly competent CGM says its simple entry visa for a foreign citizen is obtained online, at Melchior Ndadaye International Airport or at embassies. Because the same nationality-wide route is available at the airport, it is normalized as visa_on_arrival; the online application is an alternative channel, not a mandatory eVisa.
conditions: The simple entry visa allows a foreign citizen one entry and a one-month stay. Its airport route is expressly limited to Melchior Ndadaye International Airport; it does not establish visa issuance at every land or other air border.

The CGM portal also offers online application and embassy processing. Those alternative channels do not replace the explicitly available airport-issued route in the easiest-access taxonomy, and the portal’s online certificate/application process is not normalized as an eVisa.

The CGM airport form requests identity, ordinary travel-document, arrival, accommodation, contact and supporting information. Visa issuance and admission remain subject to purpose, documentation, health, security and border discretion.

The policy excludes Burundi citizenship, the seven foreign EAC citizen exemptions, work, study, establishment, permanent residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee and special-document routes. CGM separately displays free CEPGL and EAC entry-visa administrative categories; the latter does not change the EAC exemption, while no current membership-and-entry instrument is used to give Congo a different nationality status from its otherwise supported airport route.

Burundi Tourism lists a 70 USD per-month entry-visa charge, while CGM presents different fees for other entry categories and does not display an airport-form price. No fee is normalized; the direct airport issuance channel, not a price, is the basis for visa_on_arrival.

policies.title: Cabo Verde nationals: outside foreign visitor-entry scope
policies.summary: The published foreign-citizen visa framework does not establish visitor admission requirements for holders of a Cabo Verde passport.
conditions: Cabo Verde nationals are exempt from EASE pre-registration; their international-passport holders are also exempt from TSA.

A natural-born Cabo Verdean travelling on a foreign passport, and qualifying spouse or descendant, has a distinct evidence-based exemption; this citizenship evidence is not a nationality-wide foreign-passport rule.

policies.title: Listed foreign nationalities: visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Portal Único's current visa-exemption schedule expressly lists these nationalities and their maximum exemption periods. EASE pre-registration and the Airport Security Tax remain separate travel/security formalities, not an ETA or visa decision.
conditions: The maximum exemption is 30 days for AD, AT, BE, BR, BG, CA, CN, HR, CY, CZ, DK, EE, FI, FR, DE, GR, HK, HU, IS, IE, IT, LV, LI, LT, LU, MT, MC, MA, NL, NO, PL, PT, RO, SM, SG, SK, SI, ZA, ES, SE, CH, TL, GB, US and VA; 60 days for RU and ST; 90 days for BJ, BF, GM, GH, GN, CI, LR, MO, ML, NE, NG, KR and TG; and 180 days for AO, GW, MZ and UA.

Before travel, the schedule directs listed citizens to pre-register through EASE and, where applicable, pay TSA up to five days before arrival. The consular FAQ describes pre-registration as supplying flight, exit and accommodation data for prior security verification; it is not described as an authorization or visa grant, so this policy remains visa_free rather than eta.

The consular portal says foreign travellers generally must pre-register and pay TSA, but exempts Cabo Verde nationals/natural-born persons and foreign legal residents from pre-registration. TSA exemptions include children under two, qualifying official missions, forced technical/weather landings and airport transit.

The exemption schedule says a stay beyond the stated period requires a visa from the nearest Cabo Verde embassy or consular post. The general visitor framework requires a passport valid at least three months at the time of stay.

This ordinary-passport nationality policy does not determine admission for residents, laissez-passer holders, foreign-mission or international-organization staff, refugee travel-document holders, natural-born Cabo Verdeans travelling on another passport, diplomatic/official/courtesy travel, residence, work, crew or transit cases.

policies.title: Listed foreign nationalities: advance visa required
policies.summary: Portal Único's current compulsory-visa schedule says these citizens must obtain a visa at the nearest Cabo Verde embassy or consular post before travelling. The official materials do not establish a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival or eVisa route for this cohort.
conditions: Obtain the entry visa before travel at the nearest Cabo Verde embassy or consular post, then pre-register on EASE and, where applicable, pay TSA up to five days before arrival.

The consular FAQ says visa applications use an internet platform and may exceptionally be made at embassies, consular posts or in Cabo Verde with a surcharge. That generic processing statement does not prove that every listed nationality receives an eVisa, so the classification is not evisa.

The consular portal's frontier-visa statement is limited to citizens resident in countries where Cabo Verde has no diplomatic representation; it is not a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival rule for this policy cohort.

Tourism visas cover recreation and cruises, are to be used within 60 days of grant, permit 90 days and may be extended up to an equal period. Transit visas are distinct, last four days and may be extended once. Official, diplomatic, courtesy, temporary and residence visas have separate purpose and duration rules.

This policy does not override valid-residence, free-movement/agreement, laissez-passer, foreign-mission/organization staff, refugee-travel-document, natural-born Cabo Verdean family, diplomatic/official, transit, work, study or residence exceptions.

policies.title: Cambodia: named ASEAN ordinary passports visa-exempt
policies.summary: Cambodia’s current official eVisa tourist information expressly lists these nationalities in its visa-exemption cohort.
conditions: The official eVisa information names this visa-exemption cohort but does not state a common stay period. Current bilateral and arrival-service material contains nationality-specific duration data; confirm the applicable duration and entry conditions with Immigration before travel.

This is an ordinary-passport visitor finding only. It does not determine work, residence, extensions, repeated entries, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, alien or other special-document treatment.

Cambodia e-Arrival is an immigration, health and customs declaration. It is not an ETA or visa and does not turn this visa-free policy into an ETA. The current eVisa page calls it required, while GDI says it can be submitted within seven days before or on arrival.
Admission, passport validity, available ports, public-health, security and immigration-officer assessment remain separate requirements.

policies.title: Cambodia: temporary PRC, HKSAR and Macao tourist visa exemption
policies.summary: The current official eVisa announcement temporarily exempts PRC, HKSAR and Macao passport holders from Tourist Visa T for stays up to 14 days.
conditions: The announcement applies to Chinese citizens holding PRC passports, including Hong Kong and Macao SAR passports, regardless of departure point; it permits multiple entries of up to 14 days each in the stated period.
The exemption concerns Tourist Visa T only. It does not establish work, residence, ordinary/business Visa E, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, alien or other special-document rights.
Cambodia e-Arrival remains an arrival declaration, not an ETA or visa; the official temporary-exemption notice requires its completion before entry.
This time-limited measure expires after 15 October 2026 unless Cambodia officially extends or replaces it. Admission remains discretionary.

policies.title: Ten named ordinary passports: Cambodia advance Tourist Visa T
policies.summary: The current Cambodian Embassy visitor guidance expressly requires these named ordinary passport holders to obtain their entry visa before departure; it does not establish a nationality-wide eVisa or visa-on-arrival route for them.
conditions: The official Embassy list names Afghanistan, Algeria, Saudi Arabia, Bangladesh, Iran, Iraq, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Sudan and Nigeria as passports for which an entry visa before departure must be issued by the Embassy. This is an advance visa classification, not an eVisa or visa on arrival finding.

Tourist Visa T is single entry, valid for three months from issue, permits a 30-day stay, and cannot be changed or used for employment. Its extension and any other purpose or residence route are outside this baseline.

The page requires a passport valid for six months after departure from Cambodia; the Embassy's prior-visa application also asks for travel, accommodation and residence documentation. Admission and visa issuance remain discretionary.
Cambodia e-Arrival is a separate immigration, health and customs declaration. It may be submitted within seven days before or on arrival and does not convert this route into an ETA or eVisa.

This policy concerns national ordinary passports only. It does not establish Visa E/business, group, transit, diplomatic, official, service, courtesy, K-visa/Khmer-origin, refugee, alien or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: CEMAC and Nigerian ordinary passports: Cameroon visa-free short visit
policies.summary: CEMAC’s current official material says visa-free free movement of its Member-State citizens is effective; this maps the five foreign CEMAC passports. A separate Presidency source directly supports the Cameroon–Nigeria bilateral exemption for a three-month stay. Neither source supports a visa-on-arrival or electronic-visa classification.
conditions: The CEMAC policy applies only to ordinary nationals of the five foreign Member States; it is not an extension of special, diplomatic or service-passport agreements. Admission, passport, health, security and border controls remain applicable.

The Cameroon–Nigeria bilateral source supports a stay or residence of up to three months with visa exemption. It is treated as a short-visitor exemption; its continued operation should be rechecked if the agreement or its implementing practice changes.
Do not apply this policy to employment, long-term residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee or other special-document routes.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Cameroon online advance visa approval
policies.summary: Cameroon’s official Ministry and Prime Minister sources establish a compulsory online visa-file process for users travelling to Cameroon. MINREX says approval produces an online visa-issuance authorisation with a QR code before travel; the physical visa is then affixed at the border or competent mission. This is electronic advance approval, not an airport visa application or an ETA.
conditions: Apply through the official evisacam.cm portal before travel: create an account, enter the application, upload supporting documents, pay online and await processing by the competent diplomatic mission or consular post.

For applicants distant from a competent post, MINREX says the online QR-code visa-issuance authorisation permits travel and the visa is affixed at the entry border post. Applicants near the competent post may instead attend biometric enrolment. In both cases, approval precedes travel; the border step does not make this visa_on_arrival.

MINREX indicates normal processing within 72 hours after preregistration and express processing within 24 hours, but issuance is discretionary and individual documentary, health, security and admission requirements remain applicable.

The short-stay visa may serve temporary visitors travelling as tourists or businesspersons and cannot exceed six months. Work, study, residence, transit, family, diplomatic, official, service, courtesy, refugee and other special-document cases are separate.
The current review found no ordinary-passport nationality-wide arrival-visa cohort. The airport/border affixing mechanism is conditional on an approved online authorisation.

application.label: Cameroon official eVisa portal
application.processingTime: MINREX states 72 hours after preregistration for the normal process and 24 hours for express processing; neither guarantees grant.
steps: Create an account at the official evisacam.cm portal and complete the online visa application.
Upload the requested supporting documents and pay the required online fee.

Await the competent mission or consular post’s decision. Travel only with the issued QR-code visa-issuance authorisation, then complete visa affixing at the specified entry border post or competent mission.

policies.title: Foreign CEMAC ordinary passports: Central African Republic visa-free short entry
policies.summary: CEMAC's current Commission material says visa-free movement for Member-State citizens is effective. This directly maps the five other current CEMAC member-state ordinary passports to visa-free entry to the Central African Republic; no current CAR source was found to extend that rule beyond the bloc.
conditions: Applies only to nationals holding ordinary passports of the five other current CEMAC Member States: Cameroon, Republic of the Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea and Chad.
The current CEMAC publication establishes visa-free movement but does not itself publish a CAR-specific visitor duration, accepted-document, port or fee schedule. None is inferred here.

Work, establishment, long-term residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee and other special-document arrangements are outside this ordinary short-visitor policy. Passport, health, public-order, security and individual admission controls may still apply.

policies.title: Current named ordinary passports: Chad visa-free entry
policies.summary: The live official eVisa service expressly lists these 21 passport issuers as exempt from an entry visa. The CEMAC sources independently corroborate the five foreign CEMAC members within that list; no residual eVisa or visa-required route is inferred.
conditions: The official eVisa page displays this exact named exemption list. It does not state an ordinary-versus-special-passport distinction, stay period, purpose, effective date, port or underlying bilateral instrument; the ordinary-passport mapping is therefore medium confidence.

For Cameroon, the Republic of the Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea and the Central African Republic, current CEMAC material separately confirms visa-free free movement. The Convention describes tourist movement up to three months with a valid/recently-expired national identity card or passport and an international health booklet.

The official portal says all new visa applications are online as of 11 May 2026, but a generic application workflow does not prove a route for any unlisted passport. The inaccessible 2025 Official Journal PDF was not relied upon for a residual default.
Border, public-health, security, individual-admissibility, work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee and special-document rules remain separate.

policies.title: Chile: named ordinary passports exempt from transient-stay visa
