policies.summary: Chile’s current consular transient-stay schedule expressly marks these named nationality rows “NO” under whether a transient-stay visa is required. This is a visa-free short-visitor baseline, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The current schedule directly assigns these nationality rows “NO” under the column asking whether a transient-stay visa is required; it is not an inferred complement.
The schedule’s maximum stay and any note vary by nationality. This candidate records only the ordinary-passport short-visitor access status and does not impose a uniform duration.
The Tourist Card is issued by PDI to people who have already entered as tourists; it is not an ETA, eVisa or visa on arrival.
Residence, third-country-visa, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, territory, special-document and final-admission cases are excluded.

policies.title: Chile: named ordinary passports require advance transient-stay visa
policies.summary: Chile’s current consular transient-stay schedule expressly marks these named nationality rows “SI” under whether a transient-stay visa is required. The authoritative process says a prior authorization or visa is granted by Chilean consulates, so the normalized baseline is visa_required rather than eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The current schedule directly assigns these nationality rows “SI” under the column asking whether a transient-stay visa is required; it is not an inferred complement.
Chile’s authority describes the authorization or visa as granted by a Chilean consulate. Submitting material through the consular platform does not by itself make the route an eVisa.
The schedule’s conditional exemptions for specified holders of foreign visas, Green Cards or permanent residence are not used to change a passport-wide baseline.

No nationality-wide visa-on-arrival, ETA or eVisa route is established by the cited schedule. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, territory, special-document and final-admission cases are excluded.

policies.title: Current bilateral ordinary-passport visa exemptions
policies.summary: China MFA's current mutual-agreement register expressly records ordinary-passport coverage for these foreign passports; the register is the current source for each agreement's entry-into-force date.
conditions: The current MFA register records these remaining ordinary-passport agreement effective dates: MV 2022-05-20; MU 2013-10-31; QA 2018-12-21; WS 2025-04-02; SM 1985-07-22; RS 2017-01-15; SC 2013-06-26; SG 2024-02-09; SB 2024-12-28; SR 2014-05-06; TH 2024-03-01; TO 2016-08-19; AE 2018-01-16; UZ 2025-06-01.
The register says specified valid passports are permitted stays of less than 30 days; a longer stay requires residence formalities under local rules.

This ordinary-passport visitor normalization does not establish work, study, residence, transit-only, tour-group, port-visa, diplomatic, official, service, public-affairs, special-document, security, or individual-admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Forty-eight unilateral ordinary-passport visa waivers through 2026
policies.summary: The current NIA list and MFA FAQ establish a 30-day unilateral ordinary-passport waiver for these 48 nationalities, effective only through 31 December 2026.
conditions: For a valid ordinary passport only, and for business, tourism, visits to relatives or friends, exchange visits, or transit, up to 30 days calculated from the day after entry.
The FAQ says the waiver applies at sea, road and air ports open to foreign nationals unless law, regulation or a bilateral arrangement provides otherwise.
Work, study, news coverage and similar purposes require a visa in advance; border authorities still examine purpose and admissibility.
It does not establish residence, special-document, diplomatic/official, Hainan/regional, port-visa, or transit-only treatment.

policies.title: Brunei ordinary passports: unilateral visa waiver without stated expiry
policies.summary: China MFA's current FAQ places Brunei in the current unilateral 30-day ordinary-passport waiver and states no expiry date.
conditions: For a valid ordinary passport only, and for business, tourism, visits to relatives or friends, exchange visits, or transit, up to 30 days calculated from the day after entry.
The current FAQ states no expiry date; it does not make the waiver permanent by treaty or remove the authority to amend it.
Work, study, news coverage, residence, special documents, diplomatic/official travel, regional programmes, port visas, security and individual admissibility remain separate.

policies.title: Russia ordinary passports: unilateral visa waiver through 2027
policies.summary: China MFA's current FAQ places Russia in the current unilateral 30-day ordinary-passport waiver through 31 December 2027.
conditions: For a valid ordinary passport only, and for business, tourism, visits to relatives or friends, exchange visits, or transit, up to 30 days calculated from the day after entry.
The FAQ confirms the unilateral waiver applies to individuals as well as tour groups; this policy does not normalize the separate bilateral authorized-tour-group arrangement.
Work, study, news coverage, residence, special documents, diplomatic/official travel, regional programmes, port visas, security and individual admissibility remain separate.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: advance visa required baseline
policies.summary: The Exit and Entry Administration Law requires foreigners to apply to visa authorities abroad unless a legal exception applies. The current unilateral and mutual official schedules establish the covered ordinary-passport exceptions above; this policy records the nationwide short-visitor baseline for all remaining foreign catalog passports except special PRC/HK/Macao/Taiwan cases retained as unresolved.
conditions: Apply to the Chinese visa-issuing authority abroad for the ordinary visa appropriate to the actual visitor purpose; authorities can require application information, an interview and, where required, a written invitation.

This is the nationwide ordinary-passport baseline only. It excludes residence-permit holders, 24-hour and State Council transit arrangements, regional/Hainan programmes, authorized tour groups, port visas, crew, diplomatic/official/service/public-affairs/special documents, and emergency or other narrow statutory routes.

A visa can be refused for statutory security, public-order, health, fraud, financial-guarantee, documentation and other listed grounds; entry remains subject to border inspection and individual admissibility.

policies.title: Colombia: citizenship treatment
policies.summary: A Colombian citizen returns under Colombian citizenship and national-document rules rather than the foreign visitor-visa framework.
conditions: Colombian citizens have the right to enter and must identify themselves as Colombian when they also hold another nationality.
Check-Mig is optional and recommended; it is not an ETA or entry authorization.
Does not determine dual-national documentation, passport validity, minors' exit consent or case-specific border circumstances.

policies.title: Colombia: list A ordinary passports are visa-free for qualifying short stays
policies.summary: The current amended list A exempts these ordinary-passport nationalities from a visa for qualifying short non-remunerated visits.
conditions: Short stays cover qualifying non-remunerated activities such as tourism, leisure, business, events or cultural interest; paid services, salary or wages in Colombia require a visa with the appropriate permission.
The normal short-stay period is less than 90 days and may be extendable up to 180 days when the applicable rules permit it.
Admission remains discretionary and subject to a valid travel document, onward travel, funds, purpose, immigration control and any health, security or individual-admissibility requirements.
Does not classify transit, work, study, residence, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, emergency, laissez-passer, national-identity-card or other special-document routes.

policies.title: Colombia: HKSAR passport short-stay exemption
policies.summary: The current list B exempts a Hong Kong Special Administrative Region passport from a visa for qualifying short non-remunerated visits.
conditions: Applies to the HKSAR passport entry in list B, not every document associated with Hong Kong or the People's Republic of China.

Short stays cover qualifying non-remunerated activities such as tourism, leisure, business, events or cultural interest; paid services, salary or wages in Colombia require a visa with the appropriate permission.
The normal short-stay period is less than 90 days and may be extendable up to 180 days when the applicable rules permit it.
Admission remains discretionary and subject to a valid travel document, onward travel, funds, purpose, immigration control and any health, security or individual-admissibility requirements.
Does not classify transit, work, study, residence, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, emergency, laissez-passer, national-identity-card or other special-document routes.

policies.title: Colombia: electronic visitor visa unless conditional exemption is met
policies.summary: These ordinary-passport nationalities need Colombia's electronic Visitor visa unless they meet the official third-country residence or visa condition for short-stay exemption.
conditions: Visa-free entry may be authorized with a valid residence permit from a Schengen state or the United States, or a Schengen or United States visa valid for at least 180 days at entry.
Qualifying Nicaraguan natives of the North or South Caribbean Coast Autonomous Regions have an additional conditional short-stay exemption.
Without the stated evidence, nationality alone does not establish visa-free admission, so the baseline remains electronic visa.
The Foreign Ministry normally processes and issues the visa electronically, but may require a printed passport label when it considers that necessary.

Short stays cover qualifying non-remunerated activities such as tourism, leisure, business, events or cultural interest; paid services, salary or wages in Colombia require a visa with the appropriate permission.
The normal short-stay period is less than 90 days and may be extendable up to 180 days when the applicable rules permit it.
Admission remains discretionary and subject to a valid travel document, onward travel, funds, purpose, immigration control and any health, security or individual-admissibility requirements.
Does not classify transit, work, study, residence, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, emergency, laissez-passer, national-identity-card or other special-document routes.

application.label: Apply through Colombia's official SITAC electronic visa service
application.processingTime: The Foreign Ministry allows up to 30 calendar days for a decision after a complete application and study-fee payment; external consultations can take longer.
steps: Confirm that the planned activity requires a Visitor visa and choose the Colombian consular office responsible for the applicant's place of legal residence.
Complete the official online form, upload the required passport page, photograph and supporting documents, and pay the study fee.
Respond to any request through SITAC and, if approved, pay the issuance fee within the stated deadline.
Receive the electronic visa at the registered email address and travel with the same passport; a visa permits travel to request entry but does not guarantee admission.

policies.title: Colombia: other ordinary passports require an electronic Visitor visa
policies.summary: Ordinary-passport nationalities outside the current unconditional and conditional short-stay exemptions must obtain Colombia's electronic Visitor visa before travel.
conditions: A separate visa-free exception may apply to a qualifying permanent resident of a Pacific Alliance or Andean Community state, or under a current bilateral agreement; nationality alone does not establish those status-based routes.

The Foreign Ministry conducts study, processing and issuance virtually and sends the approved electronic visa to the registered email address; it may require original documents, an interview or, when it considers necessary, a printed passport label.

Short stays cover qualifying non-remunerated activities such as tourism, leisure, business, events or cultural interest; paid services, salary or wages in Colombia require a visa with the appropriate permission.
The normal short-stay period is less than 90 days and may be extendable up to 180 days when the applicable rules permit it.
Admission remains discretionary and subject to a valid travel document, onward travel, funds, purpose, immigration control and any health, security or individual-admissibility requirements.
Does not classify transit, work, study, residence, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, emergency, laissez-passer, national-identity-card or other special-document routes.

application.label: Apply through Colombia's official SITAC electronic visa service
application.processingTime: The Foreign Ministry allows up to 30 calendar days for a decision after a complete application and study-fee payment; external consultations can take longer.
steps: Confirm that the planned activity requires a Visitor visa and choose the Colombian consular office responsible for the applicant's place of legal residence.
Complete the official online form, upload the required passport page, photograph and supporting documents, and pay the study fee.
Respond to any request through SITAC and, if approved, pay the issuance fee within the stated deadline.
Receive the electronic visa at the registered email address and travel with the same passport; a visa permits travel to request entry but does not guarantee admission.

policies.title: Costa Rica: 2025 first and second group ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: Resolution AJ-484-11-2025 expressly places these nationalities in the first or second visa-free group. Only catalog country codes are mapped; territory/dependency wording conditioned on another country’s passport is not expanded.
conditions: First-group admission is up to 180 days non-extendable, subject to the stated limited extension rule; second-group admission is up to 30 days, extendable up to 90.

First-group passports require the directive’s stated validity; second-group passports require at least 90 days. Honduras has a police-certificate condition; Salvador and Russia have their expressly stated special rules.

Machine-readable/biometric document, funds, return/onward ticket and admission controls apply. No residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document or individual treatment is established.

policies.title: Costa Rica: consular, restricted and residual foreign ordinary passports require advance visa
policies.summary: Resolution AJ-484-11-2025 expressly puts named nationalities into consular or restricted groups and puts every country not named in a group into the restricted group. The normalized baseline is advance visa required; this is not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: Third-group consular visas and fourth-group Commission-authorized restricted visas are single-entry, passport-stamped advance visas; both normally allow up to 30 days subject to the directive.

The directive’s special China, Colombia, Nicaragua and Venezuela provisions and all US/Canada/Japan/Schengen/EEA/UK multiple-entry visa or residence-document exceptions are conditional and are not normalized as passport-wide access.

Passport validity, funds, onward ticket, no-entry-ban and border admissibility requirements apply. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service and special-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: ECOWAS and AES-transition ordinary passports: Côte d’Ivoire short-visit visa exemption
policies.summary: The current ECOWAS roster identifies Côte d’Ivoire and eleven foreign current Member States. The ECOWAS Protocol provides their citizens visa-free entry for up to 90 days. Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are no longer roster members, but ECOWAS's still-current withdrawal directive expressly continues their visa-free movement rights until further notice. This is a visa exemption, not an airport visa or electronic-visa route.
conditions: The Protocol requires a valid travel document and international health certificate, requires entry through an official point, and sets a 90-day visitor limit; a longer stay needs permission from the competent authority.

A Member State may refuse admission to a Community citizen classed as an inadmissible immigrant under its laws. Border, health, identity, security and individual-admissibility controls therefore remain applicable.

The current roster excludes BF, ML and NE following their 29 January 2025 withdrawal. ECOWAS nevertheless directs relevant authorities to continue their citizens' visa-free movement rights until further notice. Their ordinary-passport treatment is conditional on the official transition arrangement, including recognition of national passports or identity cards bearing the ECOWAS logo; it must be rechecked if ECOWAS announces final future-relation modalities.
This policy does not normalize residence, employment, diplomatic, official, service, UN laissez-passer, refugee, special-document, transit or event-specific access.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: statutory no-visa visits
policies.summary: The 2019 Visa Exemption Regulations expressly exempt these named ordinary-nationality passport holders from the visa default for visitor stays not exceeding six months.
conditions: S.R.O. 37 of 2019 establishes the visa default and expressly names this ordinary-passport cohort for visits not exceeding six months.

The current Government guidance confirms a no-visa route but describes some named countries as three-month visitors rather than six-month visitors. Status is supported; the conflicting duration must be checked with Immigration before travel.

The 2025 and 2026 official amending PDFs establish that the 2019 Regulations have been amended, but the publicly accessible PDFs truncate before the inserted text. They are not used to infer any additional ordinary-passport nationality or duration.
The online ED Card is a free Immigration and Customs declaration, not an ETA or visa. Visa-free status does not remove border, health, customs, security or admission requirements.
This policy excludes residence, work, study, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, and other non-short-visitor routes.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: conditional 21-day tourist exemption
policies.summary: The current Government entry guidance expressly says any bona fide tourist or transit passenger with a return ticket may enter without a visa when the Immigration Officer is satisfied that the stay will not exceed 21 days.
conditions: This is an express, conditional short-visitor route: the traveller must be a bona fide tourist or in transit, possess a return ticket, and satisfy the Immigration Officer that the intended stay does not exceed 21 days.

The status does not establish a stay longer than 21 days, work, study, residence, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, special-document or other purpose. The Immigration Officer retains the stated satisfaction test.

The 2019 statutory default requires a visa unless an exemption applies. The currently accessible Government guidance independently reproduces this all-tourist 21-day exemption; it is not inferred from visa-form availability or nationality-list omission.

The 2025 and 2026 amendment PDFs are published but truncate before the inserted provisions. No claimed status relies on guessing their nationality or document scope; their existence is a material recheck risk.
The online ED Card is a free Immigration and Customs declaration, not an ETA or visa.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: advance Dominican tourist visa
policies.summary: DGII expressly says tourists from these named countries cannot enter with a Tourist Card and must obtain a visa at a Dominican diplomatic mission. The MIREX service describes the corresponding consular tourist-visa route.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport tourist baseline only. DGII says the named nationalities must request a visa at a Dominican diplomatic mission; MIREX describes a consular tourism visa, not an eVisa or visa on arrival.

MIREX states that Decree 691-07 lets a traveller with permanent residence or a valid multiple-entry visa for the United States, Schengen/EU area, Canada, or the United Kingdom enter for tourism with a Tourist Card. That third-country-document exception does not make any listed passport nationality unconditionally visa-free.

The consular tourism visa is stated as 60 days and one entry, or 60 days and two entries for the multiple variant; applications, passport validity, financial evidence, purpose, security screening and final admission remain required.

Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Montenegro, Mongolia and Papua New Guinea are excluded because the live MIREX ordinary-passport selector contradicts this DGII list without a reconciled current instrument. Morocco is excluded because a separately listed, in-force bilateral ordinary tourism/business visa waiver controls.
This policy does not establish work, business, study, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, border-card, refugee, stateless, emergency, or other special-document treatment.

application.label: Dominican Republic consular tourist visa service
application.processingTime: MIREX states a 10-to-20-business-day response time for the visa service.
steps: Contact the Dominican embassy or consulate serving the applicant's residence or designated jurisdiction.
Submit the tourism-visa application, valid passport and the stated supporting evidence to the competent consular service.
Travel only after the visa is issued and complete the separate DGM e-Ticket declaration.

policies.title: Other ordinary passports: Tourist Card without consular visa
policies.summary: DGII expressly provides that nationals not in its named visa-required list enter with a Tourist Card. The card permits tourism without a consular visa; it is an entry tax/formality, not an ETA or visa on arrival.
conditions: Tourist purposes only; DGII states the Tourist Card gives a maximum 30-day stay, with extension administered by DGM. A person who undertakes lucrative activity loses its use and must hold the suitable visa.

The Tourist Card is a US$10 entry tax/formality, included in airline tickets issued outside the Dominican Republic for air arrivals; it may be purchased at land or sea points. It is not an electronic travel authorization, eVisa, or a visa issued at the border.

The DGM e-Ticket is a separate mandatory online entry-and-exit declaration for every passenger, not an ETA or visa. Passport validity, return/onward travel, border screening and admission remain applicable.

HK and MO represent only the ordinary Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passport routes respectively; this policy does not establish a route for other PRC, SAR, diplomatic, official, service or special travel documents.

South Sudan is excluded because the DGII residual rule conflicts with the live MIREX ordinary-passport selector. Latvia, Romania and Samoa are separately excluded because the DGII named list and live MIREX selector conflict. This policy does not establish citizenship, residence, business, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, border-card, refugee, stateless, emergency or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: Moroccan ordinary passports: bilateral tourism/business visa waiver
policies.summary: MIREX records the Dominican Republic–Morocco tourism and business visa-exemption agreement as in force from 14 July 2021. This later treaty route prevails over Morocco’s continued appearance on the DGII tourist-card visa list.
conditions: Applies to the agreement’s tourism and business waiver scope for ordinary Moroccan passports, according to the live MIREX treaty registry and ordinary-passport tourist selector.

The reviewed registry does not state a stay limit, activity conditions beyond the treaty title, document rules, or admission requirements; these remain subject to the agreement and Dominican immigration controls.

DGII’s current Tourist Card page still lists Morocco among nationalities requiring a consular visa. The in-force MIREX treaty record and selector are preferred for this direct treaty conflict; operational recheck remains warranted.
This policy does not establish residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document or individual-admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Aruba: named ordinary-passport nationalities visa-free
policies.summary: The current Dutch Government list expressly exempts these nationalities for Aruba. Jamaica is separately stated to require a visa for Aruba.
conditions: The policy is a short visitor baseline; passport validity, onward travel, purpose, funds, insurance, health, security and border-admission requirements continue to apply.

Hong Kong entries require either a British National (Overseas) or SAR passport; Macao entries require an SAR passport; Taiwan requires a passport bearing its identity-card number; Ukraine requires a biometric passport.
No residence, work, transit, crew, cruise, diplomatic, official/service, refugee, laissez-passer, third-country visa/residence-permit or other special-document rule is normalized.
For Aruba, general visa-free stay is up to 90 days in 180; Dutch, US and non-Dutch Schengen nationals may have stated 180-day allowances.

policies.title: Curaçao: named ordinary-passport nationalities visa-free
policies.summary: The current Dutch Government list expressly exempts these nationalities for Curaçao, including its Curaçao-only Jamaica rule.
conditions: The policy is a short visitor baseline; passport validity, onward travel, purpose, funds, insurance, health, security and border-admission requirements continue to apply.

Hong Kong entries require either a British National (Overseas) or SAR passport; Macao entries require an SAR passport; Taiwan requires a passport bearing its identity-card number; Ukraine requires a biometric passport.
No residence, work, transit, crew, cruise, diplomatic, official/service, refugee, laissez-passer, third-country visa/residence-permit or other special-document rule is normalized.
For Curaçao, the general visa-free stay is up to 90 days in 180; Dutch and US nationals have the stated 180-day allowance.

policies.title: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba: named ordinary-passport nationalities visa-free
policies.summary: The current Dutch Government list expressly exempts these nationalities for Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba. Jamaica is separately stated to require a visa there.
conditions: The policy is a short visitor baseline; passport validity, onward travel, purpose, funds, insurance, health, security and border-admission requirements continue to apply.

Hong Kong entries require either a British National (Overseas) or SAR passport; Macao entries require an SAR passport; Taiwan requires a passport bearing its identity-card number; Ukraine requires a biometric passport.
No residence, work, transit, crew, cruise, diplomatic, official/service, refugee, laissez-passer, third-country visa/residence-permit or other special-document rule is normalized.
For Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, the general visa-free stay is up to 90 days in 180; Dutch and US nationals have the stated 180-day allowance.

policies.title: Aruba: residual ordinary passports require a Caribbean visa
policies.summary: The current Dutch Government page supplies an explicit residual visa requirement after the named nationality and conditional exceptions; this is advance Caribbean-visa treatment, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The current official portal explicitly makes a Caribbean visa required if no listed visa-free situation applies; an application channel does not establish eVisa or visa-on-arrival access.

Valid multiple-entry Schengen/UK/Ireland/US/Canada documents and specified residence permits may waive the visa for particular travellers; these conditional routes are not nationality-wide passport classifications.
The Caribbean short-stay visa is not valid for the European Netherlands or another Schengen country, is normally at most 90 days in 180, and does not authorize paid work.
Aruba's maximum stay on a visa can be up to 180 consecutive days within 365, subject to the issued visa.

policies.title: Curaçao: residual ordinary passports require a Caribbean visa
policies.summary: The current Dutch Government page supplies an explicit residual visa requirement after the named nationality and conditional exceptions; this is advance Caribbean-visa treatment, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The current official portal explicitly makes a Caribbean visa required if no listed visa-free situation applies; an application channel does not establish eVisa or visa-on-arrival access.

Valid multiple-entry Schengen/UK/Ireland/US/Canada documents and specified residence permits may waive the visa for particular travellers; these conditional routes are not nationality-wide passport classifications.
The Caribbean short-stay visa is not valid for the European Netherlands or another Schengen country, is normally at most 90 days in 180, and does not authorize paid work.
Curaçao's stated visa stay is at most 30 consecutive days unless extended after arrival, and no more than 90 days is addressed by the short-stay framework.

policies.title: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba: residual ordinary passports require a Caribbean visa
policies.summary: The current Dutch Government page supplies an explicit residual visa requirement after the named nationality and conditional exceptions; this is advance Caribbean-visa treatment, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The current official portal explicitly makes a Caribbean visa required if no listed visa-free situation applies; an application channel does not establish eVisa or visa-on-arrival access.

Valid multiple-entry Schengen/UK/Ireland/US/Canada documents and specified residence permits may waive the visa for particular travellers; these conditional routes are not nationality-wide passport classifications.
The Caribbean short-stay visa is not valid for the European Netherlands or another Schengen country, is normally at most 90 days in 180, and does not authorize paid work.
For Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, the stated short-stay maximum is 90 consecutive days in 180.

policies.title: Ecuadorian nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: The Human Mobility Regulation's tourist-entry rules govern foreign persons, not Ecuadorian nationals presenting an Ecuadorian passport.
conditions: This classification does not establish entry treatment for dual nationals presenting another passport, residence, migration-registration, departure, document-validity, or individual-admissibility requirements.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: transitory visitor eVisa required before travel
policies.summary: Effective 1 September 2025, Ecuador's foreign ministry expressly requires the named nationalities to obtain the electronically issued Visa de Visitante Temporal de Transeúnte before entering Ecuador.
conditions: The announcement calls this authorization a Visa de Visitante Temporal de Transeúnte under the 2025 reform to Article 66 of the Organic Law on Human Mobility. It must be requested while the applicant is outside Ecuador through the ministry's official digital service.

The Foreign Ministry describes the eVISAS service as electronic visas processed 100% online. Its current guide says the approved electronic visa is sent by email for the traveller to download and present, so this is normalized as eVisa rather than a non-electronic advance visa, ETA, or visa on arrival.

The foreign ministry's visitor regulation separately provides that a tourist may not perform work or economic activity. Passport validity, visa validity, purpose, route, residence, transit, diplomatic or official document, security, prior immigration history, and border-admission requirements remain separate and are not established by this nationality rule.

application.label: Ecuador Foreign Ministry digital visa service
steps: Apply for the transitory temporary visitor visa from outside Ecuador through the ministry's digital service.
Provide the documents and pay the amounts required for the individual application.
Download the eVisa delivered by email and present it with all required documents to migration control; issuance does not itself establish admission.

policies.title: Named South American ordinary passports: visitor entry up to 180 days
policies.summary: The current exhaustive required-visa list does not include these named South American nationalities, and the Human Mobility Regulation allows South American tourists up to 180 days in a year.
conditions: The 180-day figure is the maximum that migration control may grant to a South American tourist in one year; it is not a guaranteed stay or an authorization for employment or economic activity.

The classification rests on the Foreign Ministry's explicit current list of all nationalities for which Ecuador requires a visa, read with the visitor-stay rule. It does not establish national-identity-card use, residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, or other special-document treatment.

Entry remains subject to presenting an identity-verifying travel document, migration-control verification of the invoked status, security and admissibility requirements, and any current health or carrier requirements.

policies.title: Other expressly unlisted ordinary foreign passports: visitor exemption up to 90 days
policies.summary: Ecuador's foreign ministry expressly identifies the complete current nationality list for which a visa is required; the other named foreign ordinary-passport codes are therefore visitor-exempt for the regulation's normal maximum of 90 days in one year.
conditions: This complement is inferred only from the ministry's explicit current statement that the listed countries are those whose nationals are required to hold a visa. The current source does not state a nationality-wide eVisa, ETA, arrival-visa, or electronic travel-authorization route for this complement.

A foreign tourist may remain for a maximum of 90 days from the first entry in a year and may apply once for an extension of up to 90 further days under the regulation. This normal 90-day rule does not replace the distinct South American maximum.

The traveller must present a travel document verifying identity and satisfy the migration-control officer that the claimed immigration status applies. No work or economic activity is authorized by tourist entry.

This is limited to ordinary foreign passports. It does not establish diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, laissez-passer, residence, employment, transit, special-purpose, or individual security/admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Egypt eVisa-eligible ordinary passports: visa at port of arrival
policies.summary: Egypt's eVisa portal lists this ordinary-passport cohort for electronic applications. The Ministry of Interior's port-visa schedule says that, in addition to its separately named countries, all countries previously listed in the eVisa system receive an emergency entry visa at ports of arrival. Under the easiest-access taxonomy, the nationality-wide port route is normalized as visa_on_arrival; eVisa remains an online alternative.
conditions: The Ministry of Interior's arrival list expressly adds all countries previously listed in the eVisa system. This policy chooses the arrival-issued visa as the easier available nationality-wide route; it does not erase the official eVisa alternative.

The eVisa portal describes online issuance for tourism, single or multiple entry, and requires a passport valid at least six months from arrival, the printed eVisa, itinerary and relevant hotel or visit evidence. Border officers can refuse entry even with an eVisa.
Canada's port-arrival route is independently confirmed by the Foreign Ministry as effective from 1 December 2024; the same announcement says the eVisa option was reactivated.

Purpose-specific, work, residence, study, transit, Sinai-only, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, travel-document, security and individual-admissibility rules are outside this ordinary tourist baseline.

application.label: Egypt e-Visa Portal (optional online alternative)
steps: Use the official eVisa portal to register, supply the required traveler information and pay by credit or debit card.
Download the eVisa link sent after issuance and carry the required passport, itinerary and supporting visit or accommodation evidence.
Alternatively, use the Ministry of Interior's nationality-wide port-arrival visa route where it is the easier route in this policy.

policies.title: Additional named ordinary passports: Egypt visa at port of arrival
policies.summary: The Ministry of Interior's current port-arrival schedule expressly names this cohort in addition to eVisa-system nationalities. Each is therefore normalized as visa_on_arrival, not as an eVisa or visa-free entry.
conditions: This route is an emergency entry visa granted at ports of arrival. It is not a visa waiver, an ETA, or an inference from an online form.

The Ministry page separately qualifies Iraq by age, Belize by non-Arab origin, Guinea by occupation/funds/purpose and Turkey by non-Egyptian origin; those conditional rows are intentionally excluded from this nationality-wide policy.

Entry remains subject to purpose, duration, passport, funds, carrier, public-security and border-officer requirements. Work, residence, transit, Sinai-only, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes are outside scope.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Egypt prior-visa baseline
policies.summary: The Ministry of Interior's current prior-visa schedule directly names this cohort. The six named passports that the eVisa schedule also covers are excluded because the separately documented arrival route is easier; this policy does not infer a residual default beyond the Ministry's list.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport visitor baseline from the Ministry's named prior-visa list. It does not make an online application channel an eVisa or a tourist-arrival arrangement.

The Ministry schedule records limited exceptions based on age, sex, Egyptian family links, international-organization employment, student status, GCC marriage, Jordanian residence, an accredited tourism-company guarantee, route, occupation, ancestry or sufficient funds. Those are not nationality-wide and do not alter this baseline.

Azerbaijan, Bosnia and Herzegovina, India, Iraq, Kosovo and Vietnam appear both in the prior-visa schedule and the current eVisa schedule; they are excluded here and classified under the easier documented port-arrival route. Cambodia and Thailand remain in this policy because the current eVisa schedule does not list them.
Diplomatic, official, service, crew, residence, work, transit, Sinai-only, refugee, stateless and other special-document treatment remains outside scope.

policies.title: El Salvador: CA-4 ordinary-passport entry
policies.summary: DGME expressly permits Guatemalan, Honduran and Nicaraguan citizens to enter on a valid national identity document or passport. This records the ordinary-passport baseline as visa-free.
conditions: DGME permits a valid national identity document or passport; this policy records the ordinary-passport baseline only.
A foreign traveller already in the CA-4 region must hold a passport and remaining regional stay time granted on first entry.
Residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and special-document rules are excluded.

policies.title: El Salvador: current named Category A ordinary passports
policies.summary: The current RREE table and DGME’s linked full country list expressly assign these ordinary passports Category A, meaning visa-exempt.
conditions: The DGME list uses Category A for visa exemption; country-specific notes in the table are applied where they expressly change El Salvador’s ordinary-passport category.
Australian ordinary passports require a tourist card. That entry form/card is not treated as a visa or ETA.
The table’s non-El-Salvador CA-4 notes, and rules for diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless or special documents, are excluded.

policies.title: El Salvador: Ecuador ordinary passports — country-specific Category A
policies.summary: DGME’s full current list gives Ecuador a country-specific El Salvador instruction of Category A for all passports, despite the row’s general Category B label.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport baseline from the explicit El Salvador-specific note in the current DGME list.
Diplomatic, official, service, residence, work, transit, crew and special-document cases are excluded.

policies.title: El Salvador: current named Category B/C ordinary passports
policies.summary: The current RREE table and DGME’s linked full country list place these ordinary passports in Category B (consular) or Category C (consulted), both of which require advance visa authorization.
conditions: Category B is consular/sin consulta and Category C is consulted; both are advance-visa categories under RREE’s current definitions.

DGME’s online PEI is available to Category B/C applicants, but applicants may also apply at a diplomatic mission; an approved PEI is stamped in the passport at entry. It is therefore not a nationality-wide eVisa classification.
The RREE selector can depend on a valid United States, Canadian or Schengen visa and legal residence. Those third-country-document conditions are not nationality-wide classifications.

Visa grant, duration, entries, fee, sponsoring evidence, port and admission/security controls remain case- or route-specific; residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service and special-document cases are excluded.

policies.title: El Salvador: Taiwan ordinary passports — country-specific Category C
policies.summary: DGME’s full current list gives the China (Taiwan) row a country-specific El Salvador instruction of Category C, despite the row’s general Category A label.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport baseline from the explicit El Salvador-specific note in the current DGME list.
Category C is a consulted advance visa; diplomatic, official, service, residence, work, transit, crew and special-document cases are excluded.

policies.title: Foreign CEMAC ordinary passports: Equatorial Guinea visa-free short-visitor entry
policies.summary: Current CEMAC Commission material reports that visa-free movement of Member-State citizens is effective, while its published Convention supplies the tourist conditions. This maps the five foreign CEMAC ordinary-passport codes to the easier visa-free route in Equatorial Guinea.
conditions: Applies only to citizens holding ordinary passports of the five other current CEMAC Member States: Cameroon, the Republic of the Congo, Gabon, Chad and the Central African Republic.
For tourism, the published Convention describes a stay up to three months and requires a valid or recently expired national identity card or passport and an international health booklet.

Entry remains subject to applicable border, health, public-order, security and individual-admissibility controls. It does not establish work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee or special-document treatment.
No reviewed current Equatorial Guinea authority publishes an alternative nationality-wide electronic, airport-visa or bilateral route for this cohort.

policies.title: Foreign ordinary passports: Eritrean advance visitor visa
policies.summary: Eritrea’s current Embassy guidance expressly says a visa is required for non-Eritreans. The electronic form and online fee do not result in a wholly electronic visa: applicants must mail the original passport to the Embassy and travel only after receipt of the visa. This is an advance traditional visa requirement, not an eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: This policy applies to non-Eritrean holders of ordinary foreign passports. The Embassy’s National-ID exemption for Eritreans and its special official, diplomatic, family, employment, student and transit workflows are outside this ordinary foreign-visitor policy.

Choose the visa type for the actual travel purpose. Tourist and business applications require the stated online form, photo, passport validity of at least six months, residency evidence where applicable, funds or purpose evidence, fees and the stated processing period; a family visit additionally requires an Eritrean resident reference.

The online application and fee are only consular-processing steps. The Embassy requires the applicant to mail the original passport and to travel after receiving the visa, so no nationality-wide electronic issuance or airport route is established.

The categorical non-Eritrean visa rule is published by Eritrea's Washington mission, while its document-submission workflow is specific to that consular jurisdiction. No current central nationality or bilateral-exception schedule was found; travelers must use the competent Eritrean mission's workflow.

Visas are valid for three months from issue; after arrival they are typically valid for one month and may be extended or renewed through Immigration in Asmara. Entry remains subject to health, return travel, security, prior history, document and immigration controls. It grants no work, residence, internal travel permit, diplomatic, official or special-document entitlement.

application.label: Eritrean Embassy Consular Affairs Processing System
application.processingTime: Minimum 15 business days stated by the Embassy for tourist processing.
steps: Select the visit type and complete the Embassy’s online visa application and required fee.
Provide the stated photo and supporting material, including passport validity and purpose or funds evidence.
Mail the original passport to the competent Eritrean mission; travel only once the visa is received.

policies.title: Eswatini: unambiguous N-schedule ordinary passports — visa-free
policies.summary: The current Government schedule marks these unambiguous catalog countries N (no visa required). Conflicting South Korea and same-country rows are deliberately excluded.
conditions: The source labels N as no visa required; admission remains subject to Immigration examination, purpose and other requirements.
No duration, special-document, residence, work, transit or individual-admissibility entitlement is inferred.
South Korea has contradictory source rows; Eswatini’s same-country row is not citizenship evidence.

policies.title: Eswatini: unambiguous Y-schedule ordinary passports — advance visa required
policies.summary: The current Government schedule marks these unambiguous catalog countries Y (visa required). Its Home Affairs guidance directs visa applications to the Ministry or foreign missions. The eVisa portal does not publish an eligibility list, so this status is not normalized to eVisa.
conditions: Y means visa required on the cited government schedule. The same government guidance states applications are handled by Home Affairs or Eswatini missions.
The eVisa portal proves electronic issuance for eligible countries only; it does not identify which Y countries are eligible.

The Government schedule describes a narrow, case-specific visa-on-arrival procedure after a host or tourist undertakes that prior application was impossible, while the eVisa FAQ says VOA is unavailable. Neither source maps a nationality-wide ordinary-passport VOA entitlement, so no VOA policy is asserted.

policies.title: Kenyan and Djiboutian ordinary passports: Ethiopia visa-free tourist entry
policies.summary: The live official eVisa arrival page expressly says Kenyan and Djiboutian citizens holding a valid passport can enter Ethiopia without a visa. This narrower express exemption takes precedence over those codes also appearing in the mutable arrival table.
conditions: The page requires a valid passport. It does not state a stay limit, entry count, operating port, fee, onward-ticket, funds, accommodation, vaccination or extension rule for this exemption.

This finding is limited to the named ordinary-passport visitor nationality rule. It does not decide African Union, diplomatic, official, service, residence, work, business, transit, Ethiopian-origin card, refugee, special-document or individual-admissibility treatment.
Border admission remains subject to immigration and security examination; the current eVisa general guidance reserves officials' right to deny entry.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Ethiopia tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current official eVisa service renders this exhaustive named tourist cohort with the category Visa on Arrival. The portal separately offers an online tourist visa, but an express arrival route is the easier baseline and is normalized as visa_on_arrival.
conditions: This is the official portal's current named tourist Visa-on-Arrival schedule. It does not state a universal visa-on-arrival duration, fee, passport-validity, onward-ticket, funds, accommodation, vaccination, extension, transit or work rule.

The live direct source does not identify the operating port or expressly confirm Addis Ababa Bole Airport. Accordingly this candidate records a route-limited arrival authorization but does not generalize it to every Ethiopian border or airport.

The current eVisa general information says entry officers may deny admission. Residence, business, employment, conference, study, transit, diplomatic, official, service, Ethiopian-origin and other special-document routes are outside this baseline.

policies.title: Other ordinary passports: Ethiopia electronic single-entry tourist visa
policies.summary: The official Tourist Visa page expressly makes citizens of all countries eligible and calls the visitor authorization an electronic single-entry visa. The named visa-free and visa-on-arrival cohorts are removed because they have an easier direct route; the remaining ordinary passports are therefore evisa, not an inferred consular-visa complement.
conditions: This is tourism or other non-business travel only. It is electronic and single-entry; the official page lists 30-day and 90-day maximum-duration products, and says normal processing is three days with application at least three days before expected arrival.

A recent passport photo and a passport valid at least six months from intended entry are stated requirements. The official guidance gives fees of USD 62 for 30 days and USD 152 for 90 days, with later extension procedures and overstay penalties.

The portal's global eligibility statement is explicit. Separately, it says it does not accept credit-card transactions from AF, CU, IQ, SD, SY and YE (as well as three codes already covered by the easier arrival schedule). This is retained as a material payment/access condition rather than silently reclassifying the passports as advance-visa or unresolved.

The portal says entry may be refused even to an eVisa holder. This baseline does not decide business, work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, Ethiopian-origin, refugee, special-document, health or case-specific security/admissibility rules.

application.label: Ethiopian Government eVisa service
application.processingTime: The Tourist Visa page states normal processing is three days and advises applying at least three days before estimated arrival.
steps: Use the Ethiopian Government eVisa service and choose the tourist visa for tourism or other non-business travel.
Provide the required recent photo and passport that is valid at least six months from intended entry, then complete the portal's payment and application process.
Obtain approval before travel and present the approved eVisa and travel documents for immigration examination at entry.

policies.title: Ethiopian citizens: constitutional right to return
policies.summary: The Constitution directly grants Ethiopian nationals the right to return to Ethiopia, so the same-country ordinary-passport pair is not classified under the foreign tourist visa system.
conditions: This records the constitutional citizen return right only. It does not decide passport issuance or validity, dual nationality, document checks, health, customs, criminal process, security screening or other border formalities.

policies.title: Fijian nationals: outside foreign visitor visa scope
policies.summary: Fiji Immigration says Fijian passport holders do not need a visa to enter Fiji; they are outside the foreign ordinary-passport visitor classification.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish the document requirements for a particular Fijian national, dual national, carrier, or border route.
It does not determine treatment when a dual Fijian national presents another country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: Fiji visa exemption with Visitor Permit on arrival
policies.summary: Holders of the listed ordinary national passports are exempt from obtaining a Fiji visa before travel and may be issued a Visitor Permit on immigration clearance if entry requirements are met.
conditions: Visa exemption is not a visa on arrival. Fiji Immigration calls the document issued at immigration clearance a Visitor Permit; it is issued on arrival only if entry requirements are met.

For the ordinary visitor route, Fiji Immigration describes holiday, recreational activity, visiting relatives or friends, conferences or meetings, and onward transit among the stated visitor purposes. A Visitor Permit cannot be used to seek employment or work.

The Visitor Permit period may range from several days up to four months. A holiday visitor may seek one extension of up to two months before expiry; the stated exceptions to extension include business visitor permits and students or relatives on 30-day visitor permits.

At clearance, travellers must meet current requirements including a valid foreign passport, return ticket, completed Arrival Card, confirmed Fiji address, sufficient funds, and any required fees. Fiji immigration officers retain admission and permit-period discretion.

Medical-treatment visitors and yacht owners or carrier crew must apply for their permits before arrival. This policy does not establish residence, employment, diplomatic, official, special-document, refugee, or alien-travel-document treatment.

Transit is separate: Fiji Immigration says a traveller transiting Fiji to another destination within 72 hours after entry needs a transit visa before arrival, with onward ticket and final-destination approval evidence.

policies.title: Unlisted ordinary passports: Fiji pre-entry visa required
policies.summary: Fiji Immigration's complete-list default requires these unlisted ordinary national passport holders to obtain a Fiji visa before travelling; a Visitor Permit may then be issued at arrival if entry requirements are met.
conditions: The official default is supported by Fiji Immigration's complete visa-exempt list and its express statement that all countries not on that list must apply for a visa. The visa must be approved before travel; it is a pre-entry authority, not a guarantee of admission.

Non-exempt applicants need the relevant visa before purchasing a ticket and boarding. Fiji Immigration lists sufficient funds, confirmed return ticket and accommodation among current requirements, and may require further verification documents.
A visitor permit on arrival remains distinct from the required visa and is issued only if entry requirements are satisfied. Visitor employment is prohibited.

Transit, medical treatment, yacht ownership, carrier crew, joining a vessel, residence, work, diplomatic, official, refugee, alien, emergency, and other special-document situations require their applicable separate process. For transit applications, Fiji Immigration requires proof of visa or permit for the final destination.
This policy does not establish an electronic visa, visa on arrival, or a nationality-wide exemption based on a third-country visa or residence document.

policies.title: EU, EEA and Swiss ordinary passports: visa-free overseas short stays
policies.summary: French central guidance expressly exempts EU, EEA and Swiss citizens. This records foreign ordinary-passport catalog mappings only, not French citizenship.
conditions: Up to 90 days; each overseas territory remains outside Schengen and has its own visa order.
A Schengen visa alone does not authorize overseas entry.
Excludes residence, work, transit, long-stay, diplomatic, official/service and special-document routes.

policies.title: Colombian ordinary passports: five named territories visa-free
policies.summary: France-Visas names the five destinations in the Colombian exemption. French West Indies is excluded because it is an aggregate catalog label, not the page's territorial scope.
conditions: Up to 90 days in any 180-day period for tourism, business or family visits.
No policy is inferred for the aggregate French West Indies destination.
Excludes work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official/service and special-document routes.

policies.title: Foreign CEMAC ordinary passports: Gabon visa-free short-visitor entry
policies.summary: Current CEMAC sources identify Gabon and five other Member States and state that Member-State citizens’ visa-free free movement is effective. The Convention describes the tourist free-movement stay and document conditions. This policy maps only the five foreign CEMAC ordinary-passport codes; it does not use a legacy Foreign Ministry register or the eVisa portal to infer other exemptions.
conditions: Applies only to citizens holding ordinary passports of the five other current CEMAC Member States: Cameroon, the Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, the Central African Republic and Chad.

For tourism, the published Convention describes up to three months and requires the community traveller to produce a valid or recently expired national identity card or passport and an international health booklet. The current Commission account confirms visa-free movement but does not independently restate the duration; verify the Convention’s continuing implementation before relying on that limit.

Entry remains subject to applicable border, health, public-order, security and individual-admissibility controls. It does not establish work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee or special-document treatment.
The current Gabon Government eVisa notice is limited to air entry at Libreville; it does not change this visa-free CEMAC policy.

policies.title: Gambian ordinary passports: citizenship
policies.summary: Gambian citizenship, rather than a visitor visa category, governs the home-country entry classification. The Government Passport Office page directly describes a Gambian citizen receiving an emergency passport to travel back to The Gambia.
conditions: This is a citizenship normalization for a Gambian ordinary passport, not a rule for residence, former citizenship, nationality disputes, emergency, diplomatic, service or other special documents.

The cited Passport Office material describes return by an emergency passport after loss or destitution. Passport validity, identity, security, health, border examination and other lawful controls remain applicable.

policies.title: Current GID-listed and reconciled ordinary passports: visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: The current GID table expressly lists 17 catalog passports with visa-exemption agreements and 11 ECOWAS states with free entry. The January 2025 central Government page additionally supports Cyprus, Denmark, Ireland and Latvia, which the newer GID table does not classify. This yields 32 supported foreign catalog passports; its conflicting visa/clearance rows do not establish a further route.
conditions: The GID page’s dated country entries support the 17 agreement-listed catalog codes and 11 current ECOWAS codes. Cyprus, Denmark, Ireland and Latvia are retained only because the central Government page expressly places all EU members in its waiver category and GID gives none of those four a contrary country row.

The waiver is modelled for ordinary nationality passports only. It does not establish British Overseas Territories, Crown Dependencies, Hong Kong, Macao, refugee, stateless, emergency, diplomatic, official, service, UN, residence or other special-document treatment.

The GID exemption and ECOWAS rows do not publish an exemption-stay period. The January 2025 central Government page describes the waiver visitor context as holiday or business not exceeding 90 days; duration, passport validity, yellow-fever evidence where applicable, screening, funds/onward travel, security and final admission remain subject to GID control.

The current GID table (modified 31 October 2025) puts many other EU or Commonwealth passports in visa and/or clearance groups, while the central page says the broad categories are exempt. Those incompatible scopes are deliberately unresolved; a clearance label is not normalized as visa on arrival, eVisa or a nationality-wide advance-visa rule.

policies.title: Ghana: ECOWAS ordinary passports — visa-free short visit
policies.summary: The live official eVisa checker returns no authorization for this complete named ECOWAS cohort. This is normalized as visa-free admission, not ETA, because its response expressly says neither visa nor ETA is required.
conditions: The live checker returns ECOWAS/AES, no authorization, 90 days, multiple entry, no application and no fee. The eVisa result is the current operational source; it agrees with the statutory ECOWAS exception and the Embassy's named ECOWAS list.

This policy is limited to ordinary-passport short visits and does not decide work, residence, study, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, border-pass, health, security, or individual-admissibility treatment.
Carry a valid travel document and satisfy any current yellow-fever, onward-travel, funds, accommodation, border examination and other admission conditions.

policies.title: Ghana: non-ECOWAS African ordinary passports — advance ETA
policies.summary: For this complete African Union ordinary-passport cohort outside ECOWAS and Ghanaian citizenship, the live official checker returns an advance Electronic Travel Authorization rather than visa-free admission or a visa on arrival.
conditions: The live checker labels this cohort African Union, requires ETA before travel, and returns 30 days, single entry and no fee. It is not normalized as visa-free merely because the May 2026 announcement abolishes visa fees for African passports.

The April MFA waiver table pre-dates the May eVisa launch and lists several of these passports as visa-free; the current operational checker is followed for the required authorization. This dated inter-source discrepancy is a material recheck risk.

The portal's tourist eVisa requirements require a passport valid six months beyond intended stay; yellow-fever evidence, itinerary/accommodation, purpose, security and admission requirements remain applicable. No work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document route is decided.

application.label: Ghana Immigration Service eVisa eligibility and ETA service
application.processingTime: Not established for ETA by the reviewed official source.
steps: Use the official nationality checker before travel.
Complete the required free ETA process and obtain approval before boarding/travel.
Present the authorization and supporting travel documents for Immigration examination at the port of entry.

policies.title: Ghana: named Caribbean ordinary passports — advance ETA
policies.summary: The live official checker expressly labels these ten passports Caribbean visa-waiver countries but requires an ETA before travel; the authorization is not a visa-free classification.
conditions: The live checker returns Caribbean, ETA required, 90 days and single entry. The stated message calls these Caribbean visa-waiver countries, but its required ETA controls the normalized route.

The April MFA table lists all except Antigua and Barbuda and Saint Lucia as visa-free. It predates the current electronic service and does not call itself exhaustive, so it is retained as a material dated-source discrepancy rather than used to erase the current ETA requirement.

No work, residence, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document or individual-admissibility route is inferred. Passport, health, onward-travel, funds, accommodation and border examination requirements continue to apply.

application.label: Ghana Immigration Service eVisa eligibility and ETA service
application.processingTime: Not established for ETA by the reviewed official source.
steps: Use the official nationality checker before travel.
Complete the ETA process before travel.
Present the ETA and supporting documents for Immigration examination.

policies.title: Ghana: Singapore ordinary passport — advance ETA
policies.summary: The live official checker now returns Singapore as an Asian visa-waiver country requiring a free Electronic Travel Authorization before travel. The required authorization is normalized as eta, not visa-free or evisa.
conditions: The official checker returns Asian visa-waiver country, ETA required, 90 days and single entry. The authorization must be obtained before travel even though no visa fee is stated.

The April MFA schedule listed Singapore as visa-free; its manual table predates the May 2026 eVisa launch and expressly disclaims being exhaustive. The current operational checker therefore controls the required authorization.

This ordinary-passport visitor route does not decide work, residence, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document or individual-admissibility treatment. Passport, health, onward-travel, funds, accommodation and border-examination requirements continue to apply.

application.label: Ghana Immigration Service eVisa eligibility and ETA service
application.processingTime: Not established for ETA by the reviewed official source.
steps: Use the official nationality checker before travel.
Complete the free Asian ETA process and obtain approval before boarding/travel.
Present the ETA and supporting documents for Immigration examination.

policies.title: Ghana: other ordinary passports — advance electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: For every remaining foreign catalog passport, the live official checker returns 'Visa Required' with eVisa authorization and an electronic application path. This is a true advance eVisa route, not a conclusion from online-form availability alone.
conditions: The official checker explicitly returns eVisa authorization and an application route for this cohort; embassy processing is presented as an alternative, so the easier electronic route is normalized as eVisa.

The official portal states tourist visits include holidays, visiting friends or family and short-term recreation up to three months. Single-entry visas are valid for 90 days from issuance; this is validity to travel, not a promise of a three-month admission period.

The portal requires a passport valid at least six months beyond intended stay, photograph, travel details and purpose-dependent supporting documents such as invitation/business letters. Yellow-fever, fees, onward travel, accommodation, security, admissibility, port examination and any extension rules remain applicable.

Emergency visas at entry require absence of a Ghanaian mission and advance Director authorization through a sponsor; that case-specific contingency is not a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival policy. This policy excludes work, residence, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes.

application.label: Ghana Official eVisa Application Portal
application.processingTime: The public portal advertises standard processing of 96 hours; individual approval and admission are not guaranteed.
steps: Check the nationality result in the official portal.
Create an account and submit the tourist eVisa application with passport, photograph, travel and supporting documents.
Receive and carry the approved electronic visa before travel, then satisfy Immigration examination at entry.

policies.title: Ghana: Ghanaian citizenship entry
policies.summary: The live official eligibility checker returns Ghanaian citizens as requiring no authorization, supporting the same-country citizenship classification.
conditions: The source supports only that a Ghanaian citizen does not require visitor authorization. It does not decide documentary, dual-nationality, residence, border, security or individual-admissibility questions.

policies.title: Guatemala: named Category A ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: MINEX’s current ordinary-passport classification expressly marks these nationalities Category A, exempt from the Guatemalan visa requirement. The duplicate Andorra Category A/Category B entries are not normalized and remain unresolved.
conditions: Category A travellers enter with a valid passport, but border admission remains subject to immigration control and applicable bilateral or multilateral arrangements.
The source provides no nationality-wide short-stay duration, port, fee, return/onward travel, funds, accommodation, health, extension or admissibility rule for this policy; none is inferred.
This ordinary-passport baseline excludes residence, work, study, family, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and other special-document routes.
The Category A row for the United Kingdom includes passport-wording conditions affecting British passports connected to Hong Kong. It does not directly establish the catalog’s HKSAR passport row.

policies.title: Guatemala: named Category B ordinary passports require advance consular visa
policies.summary: MINEX’s current ordinary-passport schedule expressly marks these nationalities Category B (visa consular). IGM says Category B applicants use the nearest Guatemalan embassy; the normalized baseline is visa_required, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: A Category B tourist/traveller visa is an advance mission-consular process. IGM lists a form, valid passport, photographs, travel reservation, financial evidence, international credit card and proof of payment.

The official classification carries a conditional Category B exception for holders of a valid United States, Mexican, Canadian or Schengen visa. It depends on a third-country visa and is not a nationality-wide access policy.
Passport validity, visa grant, duration, entries, fee, extension, port, onward travel, funds and final admission remain individual or process-specific unless the authority expressly determines them.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and other special-document cases are excluded.

policies.title: Guatemala: named Category C ordinary passports require advance consulted visa
policies.summary: MINEX’s current ordinary-passport schedule expressly marks these nationalities Category C (visa consultada). IGM says a Guatemalan guarantor processes it directly at IGM; the normalized baseline is visa_required, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The Category C tourist process requires advance consultation at IGM and ordinarily a form, valid passport, passport-validity certification, police/criminal-record evidence, transport ticket or Guatemalan guarantor, and payment.

IGM’s current FAQ says the United States, Mexican, Canadian or Schengen visa exception applies to Category B; Category C nationals must still obtain a Guatemalan visa. Other family, residence or document-conditioned category changes are not nationality-wide baselines.
Passport validity, visa grant, duration, entries, fee, extension, port, onward travel, funds, sponsor and final admission remain case-specific unless directly determined.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and other special-document cases are excluded.

policies.title: Guatemalan citizens cannot be denied entry and do not require a visa
policies.summary: Article 26 of Guatemala’s current Constitution directly prohibits denying a Guatemalan entry to the national territory and states that Guatemalans may enter without a visa.
conditions: This policy records the direct constitutional entry right for the same-country passport relationship; passport issuance, identification, border processing and exceptional legal controls remain separate matters.

policies.title: Guinea-Bissau: current ECOWAS Member-State citizens’ visa-free entry
policies.summary: The ECOWAS free-movement protocol gives Community citizens from the eleven other current ECOWAS Member States visa-free entry to Guinea-Bissau for a visit not exceeding 90 days.
conditions: Applies to a citizen of the named current ECOWAS Member State carrying a valid travel document issued by or on behalf of that Member State; passport code alone does not decide nationality, other travel-document categories, or dual-national document choice.

The ECOWAS Member States page retains a legacy sentence describing fifteen members, but its current named schedule and footer identify twelve. The explicit named current schedule governs this policy; Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are handled only by the separate transition policy.
Entry must be through an official entry point with a valid travel document and international health certificate. A stay beyond 90 days requires permission from the appropriate authority.
Guinea-Bissau retains the protocol’s power to refuse admission to a Community citizen categorized as an inadmissible immigrant under its laws.

Residence, establishment, work, commercial activity, family, refugee, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, security and individual admissibility rules are not normalized by this short-visitor policy.

policies.title: Guinea-Bissau: transitional visa-free entry for Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger citizens
policies.summary: Although Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger withdrew from ECOWAS on 29 January 2025, ECOWAS directs relevant authorities to continue their citizens’ visa-free movement until further notice.
conditions: The current ECOWAS instruction is expressly transitional and applies until further notice; it must be rechecked for a subsequent ECOWAS Authority decision.

The instruction requires recognition of national passports or identity cards bearing the ECOWAS logo. This policy is limited to ordinary passports meeting that document condition and does not classify non-ECOWAS-logo, alien, refugee, emergency or other special travel documents.

The source maintains free movement, residence and establishment under ECOWAS protocols; the protocol’s official-entry-point, health-certificate, 90-day visitor extension and inadmissibility conditions remain material.

policies.title: Current ECOWAS member ordinary passports: visa-free short visits
policies.summary: The PAF selector explicitly returns no visa for these current ECOWAS issuing authorities, and the ECOWAS free-movement protocol separately provides visa-free entry for a Community citizen visiting up to 90 days.
conditions: The protocol requires a valid travel document and international health certificate, entry through an official point, and a stay not exceeding 90 days; an extension needs permission.

Guinea may refuse admission to an inadmissible immigrant. Work, residence, establishment, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service and special-document treatment are not normalized by this short-visitor policy.

policies.title: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger ordinary passports: transitional visa-free movement
policies.summary: The PAF selector returns no visa for Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger. ECOWAS's current transition statement directs authorities to continue their visa-free movement until further notice after their 2025 withdrawal.
conditions: The ECOWAS transition statement says authorities should recognize the countries' national passports and identity cards bearing the ECOWAS logo and continue visa-free movement until further notice.

The policy records only the ordinary-passport visitor result. Duration, detailed entry documents, residence, work, establishment, diplomatic, official, service, border-pass, security and admission requirements remain governed by competent Guinean rules.

policies.title: PAF selector named non-ECOWAS ordinary passports: no visa
policies.summary: The live PAF nationality selector routes these seven foreign issuing authorities to its explicit no-visa result. No duration or underlying bilateral instrument is published in the selector, so the finding remains bounded to the named ordinary-passport outcome.
conditions: The selector says a foreign national needs a visa except visa-waiver countries and gives this cohort the no-visa result. It does not state a stay duration, purpose, or bilateral-instrument text.
It does not establish document-conditioned, residence, third-country visa, transit, work, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency, stateless, security or admission treatment.

policies.title: PAF normal visitor cohort: online approval followed by arrival issuance
policies.summary: For this explicit current selector cohort, the PAF service requires online approval and an Entry Visa Letter before travel, then directs the traveller to the visa-on-arrival counter for issuance and biometrics. It is normalized as eta because the prerequisite is an electronic pre-travel authorization and the final visa is issued at arrival.
conditions: The selector's normal visitor panel labels the tourist route as not exceeding 90 days. The PAF procedure requires the approved Entry Visa Letter before travel and says the final visa is obtained at the visa-on-arrival counter after photo and fingerprints.

The same published procedure lists a passport valid more than six months, Entry Visa Letter, sufficient funds, return ticket and accommodation; the service separately references a Yellow Fever certificate. Individual security, admissibility and border examination remain applicable.

This is not treated as a walk-up visa_on_arrival because prior online approval is expressly required, and not as evisa because the PAF procedure says the visa is issued at the arrival counter. It excludes work, residence, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes.

application.label: Guinea Border Police online entry-visa approval
steps: Select the travel-document issuing authority and the visitor category in the official PAF service.
Complete the online application and wait for the approved Entry Visa Letter before travel.
Present that letter at the visa-on-arrival counter, where the PAF procedure says the visa is issued after photograph and fingerprints.
