conditions: For Community citizens, the ECOWAS Protocol requires a valid travel document and international health certificate, permits a short visit of up to 90 days through an official entry point, and preserves Senegal's right to refuse an inadmissible immigrant.

BF, ML and NE are the AES States. The current detailed Category A schedule expressly continues their visa exemption until further notice; the remaining mapped Community passports are covered by the Category A schedule.

The current consular schedule separately names CF, CG, MA, MU and TN as ordinary reciprocal visa-exemption countries. It requires a valid passport, repatriation guarantee/return or onward ticket, and health certificate as applicable.
The 2026 Foreign Ministry health notice says the vaccination card is not mandatory for entrants not arriving from epidemic/endemic-country situations; changing public-health controls may still apply.

This excludes residence, employment, study, transit, refugee status, diplomatic, service, official and mission-based document treatment. Official passports and ordinary passports on official mission have distinct conditional exemptions.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Senegal advance consular visa
policies.summary: Senegal's current detailed consular schedule states that Category B requires a visa without mandatory Interior consultation, Category C requires prior Interior authorisation, and every passport absent from the lists follows Category C. This is an explicit complete advance-visa default, not inference from application availability.
conditions: Category B still requires a visa but has optional Interior consultation. Category C requires an authorisation of entry issued after application to the Ministry of the Interior; passports absent from all lists are expressly subject to the same Category C conditions.

The consular authority says the visa is issued by Senegalese diplomatic or consular authorities. This supports visa_required rather than evisa, visa_on_arrival or ETA; no current official source reviewed establishes a nationality-wide electronic or airport-issuance visitor alternative for this residual cohort.

Required materials vary by category but include passport validity of at least six months, visa form, photos, return/onward or repatriation evidence, accommodation and health documentation. Category C applicants are advised to apply two months in advance.

The current Foreign Ministry overview, retained from the 2015 regime, lists a materially broader visa-free cohort (including many European and other passports) than the detailed Category A/B/C page. The latter is used because it contains the post-2025 AES treatment and explicit Category C default; the conflict is a material review risk.

Work, residence, study, transit, refugee, diplomatic, official, service and official-mission exceptions are excluded. Issuance and entry remain subject to individual security, health and immigration assessment.

policies.title: Seychellois nationals: outside foreign visitor-entry scope
policies.summary: The visitor permit and foreign-visitor Travel Authorisation framework does not establish entry requirements for Seychellois nationals travelling on a Seychelles passport.
conditions: This classification does not establish the departure-form, carrier, document, dual-nationality, permit-holder, or admission treatment of a particular Seychellois national.
The Electronic Border System separately describes an Embarkation Information Form for Seychellois citizens and permit holders leaving Seychelles; it is not a visitor ETA classification.

policies.title: All foreign ordinary passports: no visa, mandatory pre-travel ETA and visitor permit on arrival
policies.summary: Seychelles does not require an entry visa regardless of nationality and issues the Visitor's Permit on arrival, but every foreign ordinary visitor must first obtain a Travel Authorisation/ETA before departure. The mandatory pre-travel authorization is normalized as eta.
conditions: Seychelles' Immigration guidance expressly distinguishes a no-visa system from the mandatory pre-departure Electronic Travel Authorisation. For this repository's access taxonomy, the live mandatory ETA is the operative entry status and supersedes an otherwise visa_free label; it does not turn the Visitor's Permit into a visa on arrival or an eVisa.

The Visitor's Permit is issued on arrival, initially for up to three months and free for that first period. It may be extended in successive periods of up to three months to a maximum of twelve months if the visitor continues to meet the conditions; each extension costs SCR 5,000.

A visitor must not be a prohibited immigrant or already hold a permit entitling residence; must have a valid return/onward ticket, confirmed accommodation and sufficient funds. Immigration's general entry guidance states a minimum of US$150 or equivalent per day.

The visitor route covers holiday, pleasure, business, and visits to friends/family. It does not permit paid or unpaid full-time or part-time work by a non-Seychellois; a Gainful Occupation Permit is separate. Residence, student, dependant, international-trade-zone, crew, maritime, diplomatic, transit, refugee, alien-document, laissez-passer, and other special-document cases are not established by this ordinary visitor policy.

A valid passport or other Seychelles-recognised travel document is required and must remain valid through the intended stay and return to the country of origin/residence. A yellow-fever certificate is required only for a traveller resident in, recently visiting, or transiting more than 12 hours through a listed endemic-risk country.

Use the Seychelles e-Border app or seychelles.govtas.com before departure. The current portal permits a Travel Authorisation application within 30 days of scheduled arrival and requires the passport page, traveller photo, trip information, health/customs answers and payment; permit holders additionally upload the applicable permit.

Official government pages publish inconsistent standard TA fee/application-window wording: Tourism Seychelles states €10, while MFA states EUR 10.90 and says up to 10 days before flight. Treat the live official portal checkout and current carrier instructions as controlling for price and timing; neither discrepancy changes the mandatory-ETA status.

application.label: Seychelles Electronic Border System Travel Authorisation
steps: Apply through the government-linked Seychelles e-Border app or seychelles.govtas.com before departure.
Upload the passport page and traveller photo, provide trip and required health/customs information, upload supporting trip/permit information, and pay the applicable charge.
Travel only with a valid authorization and present the return/onward ticket, accommodation and financial evidence needed for the Visitor's Permit on arrival.

policies.title: Sierra Leone: current ECOWAS ordinary passports — visa-free entry
policies.summary: The ECOWAS Free Movement Protocol establishes visa-free entry for a Community citizen visiting another Member State for up to 90 days. The current ECOWAS roster maps its eleven foreign Member States; the eVisa terms also exclude all ECOWAS members from the electronic service.
conditions: Article 3 requires a valid travel document and international health certificate and gives a maximum 90-day stay. Immigration retains admissibility and public-order controls under the Protocol.
The current twelve-State roster excludes Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger following their withdrawal; the separately documented transitional treatment applies to Burkina Faso and Mali below.
This policy does not decide residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special documents, individual admissibility or any bilateral arrangement.

policies.title: Sierra Leone: Burkina Faso and Mali ordinary passports — ECOWAS transitional visa-free movement
policies.summary: Although Burkina Faso and Mali are no longer shown on ECOWAS’s current twelve-State roster, ECOWAS’s withdrawal transition instruction requires Member-State authorities to continue visa-free movement for their citizens until further notice. Sierra Leone is an ECOWAS Member State.
conditions: This is a temporary ECOWAS transition, not a current membership classification. It remains subject to a contrary later notice, ordinary admission controls, travel-document and health requirements.

The official eVisa nationality endpoints return no electronic form for Burkina Faso and Mali. That operational result is consistent with the transition but is not the legal basis for visa-free status.
It does not establish residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.

policies.title: Sierra Leone: non-ECOWAS ordinary passports — advance eVisa
policies.summary: The current official eVisa terms expressly make all countries other than ECOWAS eligible for the electronic visitor visa. This conservative policy applies only to the 87 residual passports not named in the dated 2019 visa-on-arrival announcement; it does not rank the current route for that historic cohort.
conditions: The terms call eVisa a multi-entry electronic travel authorization, send an approved eVisa by email and require a copy at first arrival. It is a genuine advance eVisa, not merely an online form or an optional registration. Legacy portal UI wording about visa issuance at the terminal is inconsistent and should be rechecked, but does not erase the required prior electronic application and emailed approval.

The eVisa is for tourist and business purposes only, valid for one year from issue, normally multiple entry, with a maximum three-month stay and no extension. Passport must have at least six months remaining at entry; all airports and seaports are stated ports.

Biometrics are captured on arrival; funds, health, security, border examination and other entry conditions apply. The eVisa does not authorize paid employment, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service or special-document travel.

Burkina Faso and Mali are excluded here under the current ECOWAS transition; their live official selector has no forms. The dated 2019 visa-on-arrival cohort is deliberately not assigned a current status or route ranking in this policy.

application.label: Sierra Leone Immigration Department eVisa service
application.processingTime: Not established by the reviewed current official terms.
steps: Use the official eVisa portal and select nationality and visa type.
Submit the electronic visa application and payment; approval is notified by email.
Carry the approved eVisa and the same valid passport at arrival for Immigration examination and biometric capture.

policies.title: Somali ordinary passport: citizen return access
policies.summary: The Federal MFA directly provides a temporary travel document for Somali citizens who need to return to Somalia even without a valid travel document. That direct citizen-return evidence supports the catalog citizenship classification.
conditions: The source supports return access for a Somali citizen, not a foreign-entry visa classification. Identity, citizenship verification, public-health, security and border-control requirements remain applicable.
It does not model refugee, emergency, diplomatic, official, service or other special-document treatment beyond the MFA's described citizen-return document.

policies.title: Foreign ordinary passports: mandatory electronic travel authorization
policies.summary: The SCAA AIC introduced eTA for foreign passports; the later current SCAA AIP states that all arriving passengers must obtain eTA and all visas are issued online. The later all-arrivals rule controls because it does not reproduce the earlier named exceptions.
conditions: Apply through the Electronic Travel Authorization System before travel and present a valid eTA; the current AIP says all arriving passengers must do so, and the AIC warns that failure where required may result in denial of boarding or entry.

ICA describes tourist visa as one of its entry-permit categories and says the permit may be a letter, stamp or sticker. The eTA rule does not establish stay duration, entry count, fee, work, residence, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, UNLP, multiple-visa, residence-permit or other special-document routes.

The earlier 3 September 2025 AIC names Rwanda/Malaysia as visa-free and eleven ordinary-passport nationalities as visa-on-arrival. The later current AIP, effective 27 November 2025, instead says all visas are issued online and all arriving passengers need eTA, without preserving an exception list. This temporal official-source conflict is resolved conservatively in favour of the later all-arrivals operational rule and requires recheck.

application.label: Somalia Electronic Travel Authorization System
steps: Apply for an eTA before travel through the official system identified in the SCAA AIC.
Meet the ICA's passport, health, criminal/immigration-history, departure-intention and financial requirements, and provide any requested medical or invitation evidence.
Present the valid eTA and passport or travel document at the Somali border; approval does not remove individual admissibility assessment.

policies.title: South Africa: 30-day ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: DHA's current exemption schedule marks these ordinary national passports exempt for 30 days.
conditions: Ordinary national passport holders only, for bona fide holiday or business visits, and only for the 30-day period listed by DHA.
The list is subject to change without notice and individual visa exemption can be officially withdrawn, requiring a port-of-entry visa application.
This does not classify diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, crew, military, transit, residence, work, accreditation, document, purpose, admissibility, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: South Africa: 90-day ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: DHA's current exemption schedule marks these ordinary national passports exempt for 90 days.
conditions: Ordinary national passport holders only, for bona fide holiday or business visits, and only for the 90-day period listed by DHA.
The list is subject to change without notice and individual visa exemption can be officially withdrawn, requiring a port-of-entry visa application.
This does not classify diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, crew, military, transit, residence, work, accreditation, document, purpose, admissibility, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: South Africa: annual/calendar-year ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: DHA's current exemption schedule marks these ordinary national passports exempt for up to 90 days per annum or calendar year.
conditions: DHA marks these ordinary passports 90 Days P/A, defined in the schedule as per annum or per calendar year; this is not an unrestricted 90-day-per-visit rule.
For Angola, DHA additionally says each visit may not exceed 30 days.
This does not classify diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, crew, military, transit, residence, work, accreditation, document, purpose, admissibility, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: South Africa: ordinary-passport eVisa availability
policies.summary: These non-exempt ordinary-passport nationalities are on DHA's current eVisa-availability list.
conditions: Only for nationalities named by DHA's current eVisa availability page and not separately exempt under the current DHA exemption schedule.
An eVisa is still a prior visa: it is an electronic alternative to a paper visa, not visa-free admission or a visa on arrival.
Does not classify diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, crew, military, transit, residence, work, accreditation, document, purpose, admissibility, or case-specific exceptions.

application.label: DHA ePermits eVisa application
steps: Confirm the passport nationality appears in DHA's current eVisa availability list.
Create a DHA ePermits profile and complete the visa application before travel.

policies.title: South Africa: ordinary-passport port-of-entry visa required
policies.summary: The official visa baseline requires a valid visa for foreign nationals other than current exemption-list holders; DHA's eVisa list does not include these nationalities.
conditions: Ordinary national passports only, for a short visit; this is the current default where the nationality is not on DHA's complete ordinary-passport exemption schedule or current eVisa availability list.
A visa authorizes travel to a port of entry but admission remains subject to immigration examination and all document, purpose, funds, onward-travel, health, and admissibility requirements.

Does not override diplomatic, official, service, special, laissez-passer, crew, military, transit, residence, family, humanitarian, waiver, work, accreditation, document, territorial, or case-specific treatment.

policies.title: South Sudan: four MFA-listed visa-exempt nationalities
policies.summary: MFA’s current country-by-country visa-eligibility table marks Egypt, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda “EXEMPTED” with zero quoted entry-visa fees. It directly supports a nationality-wide visa exemption for the listed ordinary-passport short visitor cohort, rather than a visa on arrival or electronic authorization.
conditions: The published table does not state a duration, an effective date, passport-type qualifications, permitted purpose or entry-point limitations. This normalization is limited to its explicit country-level “EXEMPTED” rows and remains subject to ordinary border, health, security, admissibility and documentary checks.

MFA says bilateral relations can affect visa treatment. Its general page separately discusses visas on arrival, embassy processing, transit visas, and diplomatic, official and service passports; none is folded into this ordinary-passport visitor exemption.

The official eVisa portal provides a downloadable electronically issued visa for approved applicants. It is not an ETA, and this policy does not require it for the four explicitly exempt nationalities.

The Trade Information Hub’s statement that “most” travellers can obtain a visa on arrival has no nationality schedule. It does not establish an arrival-visa complement or alter the explicit MFA exemptions.

Work, residence, long stays, transit, invitation or entry-permit cases, foreign South Sudanese travelling on foreign passports, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, alien and other special documents are outside this policy.

policies.title: Sri Lankan citizenship is outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: A Sri Lankan ordinary passport belongs to a Sri Lankan citizen and is not classified through the foreign short-visit ETA or visa framework.
conditions: Does not decide a dual national's document choice, departure, residence, security screening, or individual admissibility treatment.

policies.title: 43 named ordinary passports: fee-waived Tourist ETA
policies.summary: From 25 May 2026, 40 named nationalities plus Maldives, Seychelles, and Singapore receive a fee-waived Tourist ETA. It remains an ETA requirement, not visa-free access.
conditions: The 40-country scheme expressly covers ordinary passports as well as diplomatic, official, and service passports. Singapore, Seychelles, and Maldives have reciprocal arrangements; ordinary Maldivian passports receive 90 days, while the other named free-ETA passports receive 30 days.

The free Tourist ETA permits double entry from first arrival within the 30-day validity period; on a second entry, only the balance of the 30 days is granted. A fee is due for an extension beyond 30 days.

The Department states that all foreign nationals, including the 40 fee-waiver nationalities and Maldives, Seychelles, and Singapore, require an ETA before arrival; this policy therefore does not treat a waived fee as visa-free entry.

Apply electronically through the official ETA portal. The ETA must be used to enter within three months of issue; tourist ETA is initially up to 30 days from arrival and may be extended up to six months.

At entry, ETA holders need a passport valid at least six months from arrival, a confirmed return ticket, and sufficient funds. ETA is not admission; false information, security/admissibility findings, or a referral can result in refusal.

ETA holders must not undertake paid or unpaid employment, trade, or business beyond the granted ETA purpose. Residence, work, longer stay, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, UN, special-document and diplomatic-mission rules are separate.

The official application page retains a limited BIA-only, additional-fee ETA-on-arrival facility for travellers without prior approval. It remains an approval-contingent airport fallback, not a nationality-wide visa-free rule; the published standard is ETA before travel.

A different live ETA subpage still says Singapore, Maldives, and Seychelles are ETA-exempt for short visits. The current Department notice and current ETA overview expressly say these same nationalities require ETA, so this policy follows the later current notice/overview and records the disagreement for review.

application.label: Sri Lanka ETA application
steps: Submit the Tourist ETA application and required traveller details through the official portal before travel.
Keep the ETA approval and meet passport-validity, onward-ticket, funds, purpose, and admissibility requirements at entry.

policies.title: Five named ordinary passports: sponsor-submitted ETA
policies.summary: Afghanistan, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, and Nigeria may apply for ETA through a Sri Lankan sponsor at the Department head office, rather than receiving an unrestricted online ordinary-visitor outcome.
conditions: A Sri Lankan sponsor must submit the request, sponsor affidavit, certified sponsor ID/passport copy, applicant police-clearance report, applicant passport copy, and accommodation proof to the Department head office for consideration.
This is an advance, sponsor-mediated ETA route. The alert identifies this special process but does not independently state the nationality scope of the BIA limited facility.

The Department states that all foreign nationals, including the 40 fee-waiver nationalities and Maldives, Seychelles, and Singapore, require an ETA before arrival; this policy therefore does not treat a waived fee as visa-free entry.
The sponsor-submitted ETA must be used to enter within three months of issue; tourist ETA is initially up to 30 days from arrival and may be extended up to six months.

At entry, ETA holders need a passport valid at least six months from arrival, a confirmed return ticket, and sufficient funds. ETA is not admission; false information, security/admissibility findings, or a referral can result in refusal.

ETA holders must not undertake paid or unpaid employment, trade, or business beyond the granted ETA purpose. Residence, work, longer stay, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, UN, special-document and diplomatic-mission rules are separate.

The official application page retains a limited BIA-only, additional-fee ETA-on-arrival facility for travellers without prior approval. It remains an approval-contingent airport fallback, not a nationality-wide visa-free rule; the published standard is ETA before travel.

application.label: Sri Lanka ETA portal and restricted-nationality notice
steps: Arrange for a Sri Lankan sponsor to lodge the required documents at the Department of Immigration and Emigration head office.
Await consideration and ETA approval before travel; the special alert does not establish this sponsor route as an airport process.

policies.title: Other ordinary passports: standard short-visit ETA
policies.summary: The current Department default requires a standard ETA for every other catalog foreign ordinary-passport code; the source does not create a nationality-wide visa-free complement.
conditions: The Department states that all foreign nationals, including the 40 fee-waiver nationalities and Maldives, Seychelles, and Singapore, require an ETA before arrival; this policy therefore does not treat a waived fee as visa-free entry.

Apply electronically through the official ETA portal. The ETA must be used to enter within three months of issue; tourist ETA is initially up to 30 days from arrival and may be extended up to six months.

At entry, ETA holders need a passport valid at least six months from arrival, a confirmed return ticket, and sufficient funds. ETA is not admission; false information, security/admissibility findings, or a referral can result in refusal.

ETA holders must not undertake paid or unpaid employment, trade, or business beyond the granted ETA purpose. Residence, work, longer stay, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, UN, special-document and diplomatic-mission rules are separate.

The official application page retains a limited BIA-only, additional-fee ETA-on-arrival facility for travellers without prior approval. It remains an approval-contingent airport fallback, not a nationality-wide visa-free rule; the published standard is ETA before travel.

application.label: Sri Lanka ETA application
steps: Submit the short-visit ETA application electronically before travel and await approval or a referral notice.
Carry the ETA approval and the required valid passport, return ticket, and funds to the port of entry.

policies.title: Sudanese citizens’ constitutional right to return
policies.summary: A Sudanese citizen travelling on an ordinary Sudanese passport has a constitutional right to return; this is not a visitor-visa route for foreign nationals.
conditions: Applies to Sudanese citizens; the constitutional text states that exercise is subject to law.
Does not establish a foreign-national visa route, residence entitlement, work authorization, or exemption from security and admissibility controls.

policies.title: Suriname: 21 named ordinary-passport nationalities subject to visa requirement
policies.summary: Government guidance identifies these 21 nationalities as outside the unilateral visa abolition from 1 May 2023, and BIBIS confirms that a visa requirement was reinstated for the 21 countries. This records a visa-required baseline, not an eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The Government directly names this closed 21-nationality cohort as excluded from the unilateral visa abolition from 1 May 2023; BIBIS confirms the visa requirement was reinstated for the 21 countries.

This is normalized as visa_required, not evisa: the official explanation calls the system a digital visa application system but does not establish electronically issued ordinary-tourism visas for this entire cohort. BIBIS separately says visa-required travellers may not travel without a valid visa. No visa-on-arrival route is stated.
The Entry Fee is a separate fee/voucher mechanism. It is not treated as a visa, ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival status, and it does not displace the stated visa requirement.

For Cuba, Dominican Republic and Venezuela, BIBIS says a tourist card was reintroduced alongside the visa for tourist, business and short-stay travel. The card is recorded only as an additional condition, not a separate normalized status.

The Government separately states an Entry Fee of USD 50 or EUR 50 plus a VFS Global service fee of USD 8 or EUR 8, payable at each entry; it is not a visa fee or visa category. No visa duration, entries, extension, port, admission result, health, funds or onward-travel condition is inferred. Residence, PSA, transit, CARICOM, diplomatic, service, special, official, international-organization, business, work and third-country-document exceptions are outside this ordinary visitor baseline.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa-free entry for up to 30 days
policies.summary: The current MFA schedule directly grants these ordinary passport nationalities visa-free entry, generally for up to 30 days, under listed unilateral resolutions or agreements.
conditions: The cited MFA table is passport-type-specific. This policy includes only rows that expressly cover ordinary, regular, unspecified 'without a visa', or all foreign passports; diplomatic, service, official and special-only rows are excluded.

The table gives 30 days for this group, except that Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Russia and Ukraine are separately recorded with their agreement-specific terms.

Foreign citizens with a standard visa or visa-free status must register with the stated internal-affairs or foreign-affairs bodies within the stated period, subject to agreement exceptions. Passport validity, return/onward travel, funds, purpose, port, extension, health, security and individual-admissibility requirements remain applicable.

This is short visitor-entry evidence only. It does not decide work, residence, business, transit, GBAO permits, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, border-crossing or case-specific admission rules.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa-free entry under agreement-specific terms
policies.summary: The MFA table directly records these ordinary passport visa exemptions with a 90-day term or an agreement-specific stay arrangement rather than the unilateral 30-day cohort.
conditions: The MFA schedule records Armenia, Azerbaijan and Ukraine up to 90 days; the CIS agreement rows for Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Russia do not state a day limit; Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan cite bilateral movement/stay agreements.

Do not substitute a generic 30-day limit for the cited agreement terms. Registration and all applicable admission, security, purpose, residence, work, transit, border-route and document conditions remain applicable.
This finding is limited to ordinary passports and does not decide diplomatic, service, official, special-document or individual waiver treatment.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa-free entry only for travellers over 55
policies.summary: Government Resolution No. 190, as reflected in the current MFA schedule, grants these ordinary passport holders visa-free entry for up to 14 days only where the traveller is over 55 years old.
conditions: The exemption is conditional on the holder being over 55 years old and is limited to up to 14 days. It is not a general nationality-wide ordinary-passport waiver for younger travellers.
Registration, passport validity, visit purpose, port, onward travel, funds, extension, security and individual-admissibility requirements remain applicable.
Does not decide diplomatic, service, official, special-document, residence, work, business, transit or GBAO-permit treatment.

policies.title: Moroccan ordinary passports: visa-free entry for up to 14 days
policies.summary: The current MFA schedule directly gives ordinary Moroccan passports visa-free entry for up to 14 days under Government Resolution No. 190.
conditions: The table separately gives diplomatic and service passport treatment; this policy is confined to the express ordinary-foreign-passport, 14-day row.
Registration, passport validity, purpose, ports, onward travel, funds, extension, security and individual-admissibility requirements remain applicable.
Does not decide residence, work, business, transit, GBAO, diplomatic, service, official or special-document treatment.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: advance eVisa available in the live selector
policies.summary: The official eImmigration service's live CountryForEVisa selector directly includes these passport nationalities. Easier visa-free routes in the MFA schedule are modeled separately and take precedence.
conditions: This classification rests on the live field explicitly named CountryForEVisa in the official eVisa application catalog, not merely on an online form. It is an advance application route, not a visa-on-arrival finding.

The MFA PDF says its simplified visa/eVisa requests are fee-based and may also describe visa-support confirmation or official-invitation routes. Follow the current application workflow, fees, passport, photograph, duration, entry, port and decision requirements presented during application.

The selector has a stateless-person record that is not a nationality passport code and is deliberately excluded. Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan are modeled only as the portal's named passport/nationality records, not as an inference about PRC travel documents or residence status.

Does not decide visa on arrival with support confirmation, GBAO permits, residence, work, business, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, security or individual-admissibility treatment.

application.label: Tajikistan e-Visa application
steps: Select the eVisa application route in the official Tajikistan eImmigration service.
Choose the passport nationality shown in the live CountryForEVisa selector.
Submit the application and required documents, pay the applicable fee, and await the official decision before travel.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: advance consular visa required
policies.summary: After its current named visa-free and simplified/eVisa cohorts, the MFA PDF expressly says citizens of all other countries must obtain a visa from Tajik embassies or consulates before departure.
conditions: This is an explicit official default for other foreign countries, not an inference from their absence in an eVisa list. Obtain the visa from a Tajik embassy or consulate before departure.

The classification does not collapse the separate support-confirmation/official-invitation simplified arrival process into a nationality-wide visa on arrival. It also does not claim that online submission converts a consular visa into eVisa issuance.
Registration, passport validity, purpose, duration, entries, port, fee, supporting documents, extension, onward travel, funds, security and individual-admissibility requirements remain applicable.
Does not decide GBAO permits, residence, work, business, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, stateless-person, PRC travel-document or route-specific treatment.

policies.title: Tajikistan: citizenship entry
policies.summary: Tajikistan's Constitution gives a citizen the right to travel, leave the Republic and return, supporting the same-country citizenship classification.
conditions: This is a citizenship/right-of-return finding, not foreign visitor-visa evidence.
It does not decide documentary requirements, dual nationality, residence, GBAO access, exit control, security, criminal-law or individual-admissibility issues.

policies.title: Tanzanian citizens: outside foreign-visitor visa regime
policies.summary: The Immigration Department's current entry guidance distinguishes Tanzanian citizens from foreign nationals subject to visa or visa-on-arrival procedures. The same-country ordinary-passport pair is therefore recorded as citizenship rather than a foreign visitor visa status.
conditions: All travellers must use designated formal entry points, appear to an immigration officer, complete the arrival declaration and produce a passport or other acceptable document.
This does not decide citizenship acquisition, dual nationality, passport validity, residence, customs, health, security, criminal process or individual border formalities.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Tanzania visa-free visitors
policies.summary: The 2016 Visa Regulations' Third Schedule directly names 44 of this cohort as not requiring a visa. Current eVisa group guidance directly supports the two additional EAC/SADC entries (CD and ZW); the separate detailed eVisa-list URL was unavailable on re-review, so no wider unlisted complement is inferred.
conditions: This policy applies only to the directly supported ordinary-passport cohort. It does not establish a common stay limit, work entitlement, residence right, transit rule or special-document exemption.

The current eVisa guide's broad EAC/SADC/Commonwealth wording conflicts with its own detailed VOA/referral categories and with portions of the 2016 schedules. The current detailed visa-free endpoint returned a runtime error on re-review. The 44 statutory Third-Schedule codes are retained; CD and ZW are the only additional catalog codes directly supported by the current EAC/SADC wording and not contradicted by a current named route. Burundi and South Sudan remain unresolved because they are omitted from the statutory schedule and all current detailed categories despite the EAC prose.

All entry remains through designated points with a passport or other acceptable document, arrival declaration, and possible onward-travel, funds and current health/yellow-fever documentation. The Immigration Officer retains admission authority.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Tanzania ordinary or multiple visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current official Immigration guideline expressly gives this named cohort both online and visa-on-arrival facilities. Because the same visitor visa can be issued at an official entry point, the easiest supported baseline is visa_on_arrival, not evisa.
conditions: The direct named schedule grants both online and on-arrival facilities. It does not make an online application mandatory, so this is not normalized as evisa. Issuance is only at an official designated entry point, not an assertion that every port offers an arrival visa.

An ordinary tourist visa is stated to cost USD 50 and be valid up to 90 days. United States passport holders visiting for tourism are instead required to use the USD 100 multiple visa, even for a single entry; the guide nevertheless includes the United States in the named on-arrival cohort.

The portal's raw lists overlap: Ghana, Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent are also on the live visa-free schedule, so their direct no-visa route prevails; Burkina Faso and Guinea appear in the raw VOA list but are referral cases, so the referral eVisa policy prevails. These codes are omitted from this VOA policy.

Ordinary visa holders may not work or conduct business. Transit, work, residence, business-only, diplomatic, official, service, refugee/stateless, special-document and Zanzibar-specific operating rules are not decided by this policy. Entry remains subject to documents, health, funds/onward travel and officer discretion.

application.label: Tanzania Immigration eVisa service
application.processingTime: The terms say online applications should be lodged ten days before expected travel; this does not apply where the visitor instead uses the expressly available on-arrival route.
steps: Choose either the official online visa application or the permitted visa-on-arrival procedure at an official entry point.
For an online application, submit the required documents and payment, then obtain the Visa Grant Notice through the portal before travel.
Present the required documents to Immigration. A grant notice or arrival-visa application does not guarantee admission.

policies.title: Referral ordinary passports: Tanzania advance electronic visa approval
policies.summary: Tanzania Immigration's current referral list prohibits this cohort from using visa on arrival without special Commissioner-General permission and requires an online application approved before travel. The online grant notice makes the ordinary baseline evisa.
conditions: Referral nationals must apply online and wait for approval before starting travel, unless they obtain special approval from the Commissioner General of Immigration. They are advised to apply at least two months before travel and supply local-host/contact and invitation or visa-application-letter information where available.

This policy is evisa because the official portal processes the online application and lets approved applicants download the Visa Grant Notice. It does not turn the exceptional Commissioner's permission into a nationality-wide VOA route.

The direct referral list takes precedence over the raw VOA schedule's Burkina Faso and Guinea entries. Refugee and stateless applicants also cannot use VOA but are document/status categories, not ordinary-passport nationality policies.

Ordinary visitor approval does not authorize work or business and remains subject to entry documents, designated ports, health/yellow-fever requirements, funds/onward evidence, security and immigration-officer discretion.

application.label: Tanzania Immigration referral visa application
application.processingTime: Referral applicants are advised to submit at least two months before travel and must wait for approval before commencing the journey.
steps: Submit the referral visa application through the official Tanzania Immigration portal.
Provide the passport, supporting documents, local-host details and an invitation or visa-application letter addressed to the Commissioner General where available.
Wait for approval, download the Visa Grant Notice from the portal, and present it with entry documents at a designated entry point.

policies.title: Thailand: Thai ordinary-passport holders
policies.summary: Thai citizens are not foreign nationals subject to Thailand's foreign-national visa and TDAC requirement.
conditions: Citizenship classification only; it does not determine dual-nationality, passport issuance, exit controls, residence, work, transit, or admissibility.
A Thai citizen travelling on a foreign passport is outside this passport-nationality finding.

policies.title: Thailand: current 60-day ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: The current Consular Affairs schedule gives these ordinary-passport nationalities visa-exempt admission for tourism and short-term business engagements for up to 60 days.
conditions: For tourism and short-term business engagements only, with a stay not exceeding 60 days.

The current schedule is used because it remains linked by the 31 March 2026 Consular Affairs index. The 19 May 2026 revision notice says its changes begin only 15 days after a Ministry of Interior announcement appears in the Royal Gazette; recheck before travel.
TDAC must be submitted by non-Thai nationals up to three days before arrival; it is an arrival declaration, not a visa or ETA.
Does not establish work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special-document, border-pass, extension, repeat-entry, security, or discretionary-admission rights.

policies.title: Thailand: 14-day bilateral ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: Myanmar and Timor-Leste ordinary-passport holders have the listed 14-day bilateral visa-exemption route.
conditions: Maximum stay is 14 days.
For Myanmar, the schedule expressly limits the route to international airports.
TDAC applies to non-Thai arrivals and is not a visa or ETA.
No inference for work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, border passes, extensions, repeat entry, or discretionary admission.

policies.title: Thailand: 30-day bilateral ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: Chile's ordinary-passport bilateral agreement provides a 30-day visa-exemption route.
conditions: Maximum stay is 30 days.
TDAC applies to non-Thai arrivals and is not a visa or ETA.
No inference for work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, border passes, extensions, repeat entry, or discretionary admission.

policies.title: Thailand: 90-day bilateral ordinary-passport visa exemption
policies.summary: Argentina and Brazil ordinary-passport bilateral agreements provide a 90-day visa-exemption route.
conditions: Maximum stay is 90 days.
TDAC applies to non-Thai arrivals and is not a visa or ETA.
No inference for work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, border passes, extensions, repeat entry, or discretionary admission.

policies.title: Thailand: 15-day ordinary-passport visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current Consular Affairs VOA schedule gives these ordinary-passport nationalities a 15-day visa-on-arrival route; entries with the concurrent 60-day exemption are classified under that easier route instead.
conditions: The schedule states a 15-day stay. It does not establish a nationality-wide electronic visa, ETA, or advance-visa requirement for these passports.

The current schedule is used because it remains linked by the 31 March 2026 Consular Affairs index. The 19 May 2026 revision notice says its changes begin only 15 days after a Ministry of Interior announcement appears in the Royal Gazette; recheck before travel.
Current national schedule alone does not establish ports, fees, passport-validity, accommodation, funds, onward-ticket, extension, or repeat-entry terms; verify these with Immigration before travel.
TDAC applies to non-Thai arrivals and is not a visa or ETA.
No inference for work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, border passes, security, or discretionary admission.

policies.title: Thailand: foreign ordinary passports eligible to apply for Thai eVisa
policies.summary: The MFA says foreign nationals can apply for Thai eVisa worldwide except from inside Thailand. These passports have no easier nationality-wide route established by the current schedules above.
conditions: Applicant must be a foreign national located outside Thailand; the worldwide statement establishes availability of the electronic application route, not guaranteed issuance or admission.

The portal requires an online account, application, supporting documents and payment. The competent mission may seek further documents or interview the applicant; exact visa type, purpose, document and nationality checks remain case-specific.
TDAC applies to non-Thai arrivals and is an arrival declaration, not a visa or ETA.

This ordinary-passport visitor-route classification does not establish work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special-document, border-pass, fee, duration, port, extension, security, or discretionary-admission rights.

application.label: Thai eVisa official portal
steps: Apply from outside Thailand through the Thai eVisa portal.
Create an account, select the appropriate visa category, upload the required documents, and pay the stated fee.
Await the competent mission's decision and use the approval email as instructed for travel and Immigration inspection.

policies.title: United States ordinary passports: tourism visa exemption
policies.summary: Current official traveller guidance expressly identifies United States nationals as subject to a visa-exemption arrangement when travelling for tourism.
conditions: The exemption is expressly stated for tourism. It does not establish visa-free business, work, residence, transit, study, media, volunteer, diplomatic, official, service or special-document access.

The statement appears in current air-or-sea arrival guidance. It does not independently establish a separate land-border entitlement or remove normal documentary, health, security and individual-admissibility checks.
The statutory 30-day tourist-visa duration does not itself specify the stay length of the exemption; comply with the entry permission actually granted and any current Immigration conditions.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Dili airport or seaport visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current Customs Authority page states that nationals of other countries may apply for a visa on arrival only at Dili International Airport or Dili Sea Port. This residual policy excludes the operative EU–Timor-Leste waiver cohort.
conditions: For every listed foreign passport not separately exempt, the current ordinary visitor route is a visa application on arrival only at Dili International Airport or Dili Sea Port. This policy is not a nationwide or land-border VOA finding.

Indonesian nationals may apply on arrival at any border post, including land crossings, Dili International Airport and Dili Sea Port. All other listed passports arriving at a land border must first obtain a Visa Application Authorization, present it to Immigration, and then receive a visa on payment; this advance-authorisation route is not normalized as eVisa or an unrestricted VOA.

The current page requires an arrivals card, genuine tourist or business purpose, sufficient funds, accommodation arrangements, a travel document valid at least six months with an unused visa page, onward/return arrangements, and USD 30 cash. Immigration may refuse applicants who do not meet requirements.
The Act gives tourist visas a 30-day validity, single entry, and one equal extension; a trip to or from Oe-Cusse Ambeno permits multiple entries. Tourist visas do not authorize professional activity.

Does not decide residence, work, business class II, transit, airport-transit, Oe-Cusse border-pass, visa-support/advance mission procedure, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, citizenship, security, health, criminal-history or case-specific admission treatment.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: reciprocal short-stay visa waiver
policies.summary: The operative EU–Timor-Leste agreement waives a Timor-Leste visa for ordinary passports of EU Member States except Ireland, and takes precedence over bilateral arrangements within its scope.
conditions: Valid ordinary passport; stays in Timor-Leste may not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period.
Paid activity is excluded. The agreement does not establish work, residence, long-stay, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.
The waiver applies regardless of transport mode. Entry and short-stay conditions, individual refusal, and other admissibility requirements remain applicable.
The EU agreement takes precedence over bilateral agreements or arrangements on matters it covers; the Customs page's narrower named list does not displace this operative treaty cohort.

policies.title: Timor-Leste: citizenship entry
policies.summary: The Immigration and Asylum Act expressly regulates the entry and exit conditions of Timor-Leste nationals separately from foreigners, supporting the same-country citizenship classification.
conditions: This is a nationality/citizenship classification, not foreign visitor-visa evidence.
It does not decide passport issuance, dual nationality, exit controls, residence, land-border documents, security, criminal-law or individual-admissibility issues.

policies.title: African ordinary passports: Togo visa-free short visit
policies.summary: From 18 May 2026, Togo’s Government exempts nationals of every African State holding a valid national passport. The live official portal confirms this ordinary-passport visitor route for stays up to 30 days.
conditions: Applies only to the named African passport issuers and a valid ordinary national passport, for a stay of up to 30 days.
The official portal requires completion of the immigration slip no later than 24 hours before arrival. This is an immigration formality, not an ETA or a visa.

The same live eVisa-information page retains an earlier ECOWAS-centred exemption table and lists some now-exempt African states as visa-subject. The 18 May 2026 Government decision, homepage notice and live ordinary-passport checker control; the legacy table is recorded as a source conflict, not used to narrow the African exemption.
Border inspection, security, legal controls and individual admissibility remain; residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service and special-document rules are outside this policy.

policies.title: Togo-issued ordinary passport: no foreign-entry visa in the live assistant
policies.summary: The live ordinary-passport assistant returns no visa for a Togolese passport. This directly supports only the repository's citizenship classification; it does not assert constitutional return rights or treatment of other documents.
conditions: The assistant was queried as an ordinary Togolese passport with short visitor assumptions and returns no visa. Separate identity, nationality, border, security and admission rules remain applicable.
This does not infer treatment for national identity cards, consular cards, residence documents or diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency or other special travel documents.

policies.title: Singapore and Malaysia ordinary passports: live assistant no-visa result
policies.summary: The live official ordinary-passport assistant returns no visa for Singapore and Malaysia under the short tourist test inputs. The 2026 African rule does not explain these two non-African outcomes, so they are separate and medium confidence.
conditions: The current checker returns no visa for ordinary Singapore and Malaysian passports with a short tourist stay. It does not publish an underlying bilateral instrument, duration or document/purpose crosswalk.
Separate immigration formalities, border inspection, security, admissibility, work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service and special-document rules remain outside this policy.

policies.title: Live checker non-African ordinary-passport tourist cohort: advance electronic visa
policies.summary: For this complete named cohort, the live ordinary-passport assistant returns that a visa is required. Togo Voyage identifies the product as an electronic visa, requires online application before travel, and says it avoids a border-visa queue; it is normalized as evisa.
conditions: The current assistant was queried for each listed ordinary passport with a short tourist stay and returned that a visa is required. The eVisa page's country table independently lists each as visa-subject, subject to stated bilateral or multilateral arrangements.

The current portal says applications must be made online at least five days before arrival; standard processing is five days. Its tourist table provides 1–15 day single or multiple entry, 16–30 day multiple entry, and 31–90 day multiple entry options.

Arrival and express visas are currently suspended. The portal labels the advance product eVisa, says it avoids a border-visa queue and sends confirmation by email; normal border, passport, funds, health, security and admission requirements remain.

The legacy table contains stale African visa-required rows, overridden by the separate current African policy. Work, residence, official/courtesy, diplomatic, service, transit, crew and special-document routes are excluded.

application.label: Togo Voyage electronic tourist-visa application
application.processingTime: The current portal says standard visa applications take five days and must be made at least five days before arrival.
steps: Use the official visa assistant with an ordinary passport, visitor purpose, intended arrival date and stay duration.
If the assistant says a visa is required, create an account and complete the online application, supporting documents and online payment.
Carry the approved electronic-visa confirmation and complete the separate immigration formalities before travel.

policies.title: Trinidad and Tobago nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: The Immigration Division's eVisa service applies to eligible foreign nationals, not nationals presenting a Trinidad and Tobago passport.
conditions: This does not establish treatment for a dual national presenting another passport, residence, work, departure controls, or individual border admission.

From 17 March 2026, all persons entering or leaving Trinidad and Tobago must complete the free online Arrival/Departure Card before travel (up to 72 hours) and present its QR-code receipt. This is a travel declaration, not a visa, ETA, or entry guarantee.

policies.title: Named non-CARICOM ordinary passports: visa exemption
policies.summary: The Immigration Division's current visa-exempt-country list expressly says these named nationalities do not require a visa for entry to Trinidad and Tobago.
conditions: The current official list establishes no common visitor-stay duration, work right, residence right, transit rule, or special-document treatment for this mixed nationality cohort.

This policy is confined to the named ordinary-passport nationalities. It does not extend the country list to other Commonwealth, territorial, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, crew, or travel-document holders.

From 17 March 2026, all persons entering or leaving Trinidad and Tobago must complete the free online Arrival/Departure Card before travel (up to 72 hours) and present its QR-code receipt. This is a travel declaration, not a visa, ETA, or entry guarantee.

policies.title: Named CARICOM ordinary passports: visa exemption and six-month definite entry
policies.summary: The Immigration Division lists these CARICOM nationalities as visa-exempt; Foreign Ministry CSME guidance says a CARICOM national seeking entry receives a definite six-month entry subject to immigration requirements.
conditions: The stated six months is subject to satisfaction of all immigration requirements and does not itself establish entry, employment, residence, a work-permit exemption, or an indefinite CSME Skills Certificate stay.
Free movement for listed CSME skill categories requires the appropriate Skills Certificate; other CARICOM nationals seeking employment must apply for a work permit.
This policy covers only the common ordinary-passport visitor component, not diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, crew, or other special documents.

From 17 March 2026, all persons entering or leaving Trinidad and Tobago must complete the free online Arrival/Departure Card before travel (up to 72 hours) and present its QR-code receipt. This is a travel declaration, not a visa, ETA, or entry guarantee.

policies.title: United Kingdom and European Union ordinary passports: visa exemption
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry's current visa instructions expressly say that United Kingdom passport holders and European Union member-country holders do not require visas to visit Trinidad and Tobago.
conditions: The instructions do not provide a shared visitor-stay duration or establish employment, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, or other special-document treatment.
Ireland and the United Kingdom also appear on Immigration's current visa-exempt-country list; this policy includes each code once as the explicit UK/EU group.

From 17 March 2026, all persons entering or leaving Trinidad and Tobago must complete the free online Arrival/Departure Card before travel (up to 72 hours) and present its QR-code receipt. This is a travel declaration, not a visa, ETA, or entry guarantee.

policies.title: Explicitly named ordinary passports: electronic visitor visa required
policies.summary: The current Foreign Ministry visa instructions directly identify these nationalities as requiring a visa, and state that all Trinidad and Tobago entry visas are electronic; they are normalized as eVisa.
conditions: China, Taiwan, Cuba, North Korea, and Vietnam are expressly named in the current instructions' visa-required applicant cohort; Venezuela is expressly stated to require a visa for entry. The regional references to Asian, African, Middle-East and Far-East countries are not used to infer any additional code.

The Immigration Division eVisa service is for eligible foreign nationals from visa-required countries. Applicants need a passport valid at least six months, email address, digital photograph, supporting PDFs, and a Visa or Mastercard; approval is sent by email.

The official portal currently lists a TTD 800 multiple-entry eVisa fee, while ttconnect describes a TTD 400 fee. This official fee discrepancy is unresolved and does not alter the eVisa classification.

Bona fide operating aircraft or seagoing-vessel crew do not require a visa regardless of nationality; that occupation-specific exception is not a nationality-wide ordinary visitor rule. Possession of an eVisa does not guarantee admission.
This does not establish work, residence, student, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, or other special-document treatment.

From 17 March 2026, all persons entering or leaving Trinidad and Tobago must complete the free online Arrival/Departure Card before travel (up to 72 hours) and present its QR-code receipt. This is a travel declaration, not a visa, ETA, or entry guarantee.

application.label: Trinidad and Tobago Immigration Division eVisa Online Services
steps: Confirm that the passport nationality is subject to a visa requirement and meets the online-service eligibility screening.
Prepare the required passport, digital photograph, supporting documents, email address, and payment card.
Apply through the Immigration Division eVisa portal, receive the approved eVisa by email, print it, and present it with the Arrival/Departure Card receipt to border officers.

policies.title: Turkmenistan: citizen right of entry
policies.summary: Turkmenistan’s Migration Law and current Migration Service guidance directly establish a Turkmen citizen’s right to enter with the prescribed citizen travel document.
conditions: The current Migration Service identifies the biometric Turkmen passport as an entry document; the Migration Law establishes the citizen entry right. This is not a foreign visitor visa exemption.
This does not decide dual-nationality/document choice, exit restrictions, residence, work, military, registration, security or individual border treatment.

policies.title: Named foreign nationalities: visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Uganda's live NCIC schedule expressly says nationals of these 40 listed countries or regions do not require a visa. The classification is visa_free, not a visa on arrival.
conditions: The current NCIC schedule frames the exemption as visa-abolition agreements. It does not publish a common ordinary-visitor duration, purpose or work entitlement; confirm the admission stamp and agreement-specific conditions at entry.

The archived 2021 visa-prone notice has a different 39-country list: it includes AO, CU and LY, but not the live schedule's CD, MZ, AE or HK. The live NCIC schedule controls current nationality scope; the 2021 notice supports online-processing mechanics only.

For EAC travel, the Kigali High Commission says Rwanda and Kenya citizens may enter with a valid national identity card or e-passport; Burundi and Tanzania citizens are exempt with a valid e-passport or laissez-passer. This ordinary-passport policy does not convert those alternative documents into a residence right.

A visa-exempt national holding a valid Conventional Travel Document is also exempt from the online visa requirement. Treatment of other refugee, alien, emergency or special documents is not established here.

The NCIC page separately exempts diplomatic/official passports of DZ, CU, EG, ET, IN, IR, RU, SN, ZA, TR (diplomatic only), VE and VN, plus named international-organization laissez-passers on official business. Those exceptions do not broaden ordinary-passport access.

Valid Kenya, Rwanda or Uganda resident-permit holders travelling within those territories can obtain an InterState Pass at entry; that residence exception does not apply to travel into Uganda from outside Kenya or Rwanda.
Visa-free status does not authorize employment, study, residence, work, crew, transit, diplomatic/official travel, East African Tourist Visa travel, or otherwise inadmissible entry.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: advance electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: The live complete no-visa schedule identifies the ordinary foreign passports that do not need a visa. For the remaining ordinary foreign passports, NCIC's online process requires a Travel Authorization/Visa Approval Letter before travel and does not issue normal visas on arrival; the complement is normalized as evisa.
conditions: Apply through visas.immigration.go.ug and obtain the Travel Authorization/Visa Approval Letter before boarding. The 2021 NCIC notice says there are no normal visas issued on arrival; the current Abuja High Commission page says all visa applications use the same electronic system. This is evisa rather than eta or visa_on_arrival.

The changed 2021 nationality list is not used to construct this complement: current scope comes from the live 40-country NCIC schedule, while the 2021 notice only corroborates the online approval and no-visa-on-arrival process.

The ordinary/tourist single-entry route covers tourism, medical treatment and family visits; it may be granted up to three months. The published fee is USD 50, approval is valid 90 days, and the initial period may be extended by another 60 days in two intervals.

Use a passport valid at least six months and upload the passport biodata page, itinerary/tour plan, recent photo and accommodation evidence; purpose-specific invitations/status documents and yellow-fever evidence may be required.
Carry the approval letter, passport, payment evidence and uploaded documents to border control for biometric capture. Approval does not guarantee admission; immigration decides at entry.
Transit is a separate online visa capped at seven days and non-extendable. The East African Tourist Visa and employment, residence, student, dependant and special passes are distinct routes.

This complement excludes named nationality exemptions, qualifying CTDs, EAC identity-card/e-passport or laissez-passer travel, EAC-resident InterState Passes, diplomatic/official passports, international-organization laissez-passers, British military personnel and specifically authorized temporary operational exceptions.

application.label: Uganda Electronic Visa/Permit Application System
application.processingTime: NCIC's online-visa notice says decisions take 2–3 days and advises applying at least ten days before travel; Kigali High Commission says typically 2–3 working days and recommends five working days.
steps: Start a Visa application on the official system and select the ordinary/tourist category and purpose.
Complete the form, upload the passport, photo and purpose-specific documents, and make required payment.
Receive the Travel Authorization/Visa Approval Letter and carry it with the submitted evidence to border control.

policies.title: Anguilla: live selector eVisa-eligible ordinary passports
policies.summary: The live Anguilla selector directly labels these catalog ISO2 passport codes ‘Visa Required’; the same government portal provides the electronic visitor-visa application and states that an approved electronic visa establishes travel eligibility.
conditions: Ordinary-passport visitor classification only.
An approved electronic visa establishes travel eligibility but does not guarantee admission; arrival inspection and inadmissibility controls apply.
It excludes residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document, purpose, duration and individual-waiver routes.

policies.title: Anguilla: live selector visa-not-required ordinary passports
policies.summary: The live Anguilla selector directly labels these catalog ISO2 passport codes ‘Visa Not Required’.
conditions: It excludes residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document, purpose, duration, admission and individual-waiver routes.

policies.title: Turks and Caicos: named visa-exempt ordinary passports
policies.summary: The current Border Force page expressly lists these nationalities as visa-exempt.
conditions: Valid passport and border-officer admission remain required.
Residence permits, UK/US/Canada visas, work, transit, crew, citizenship/status, diplomatic, official/service and special documents are not normalized.

policies.title: Turks and Caicos: residual ordinary passports require advance visa
policies.summary: The current Border Force page expressly says citizens outside its visa-exempt list must obtain a visa.
conditions: UK/US/Canada residence or a valid visa is conditional, not nationality-wide access.
Application is neither eVisa nor visa on arrival.
Admission, work, transit, crew, citizenship/status, diplomatic, official/service and special-document rules remain separate.

policies.title: Falkland Islands: named visa-national ordinary passports
policies.summary: The current Customs and Immigration page expressly names these nationalities as requiring a visa.
conditions: Visas must be secured in advance; the visitor permit is a separate arrival stamp, not visa on arrival.
Visitor permits prohibit employment and require onward travel, accommodation, funds and medical-evacuation insurance.
No status is inferred for omitted passports or status/document exceptions.

policies.title: Cayman Islands: current table visa-not-required ordinary passports
policies.summary: The current CBC visitor table expressly labels these named ordinary-passport nationalities ‘Visa Not Required’.
conditions: Ordinary-passport visitor baseline only.
The table’s residence, work-permit, re-entry-permit and third-country document waivers are conditional and are not normalized.
Taiwan’s listed exemption is limited to an ordinary passport issued by its Ministry of Foreign Affairs that includes the personal identification number.
Admission, duration, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service and special-document rules remain separate.

policies.title: Cayman Islands: current table visa-required ordinary passports
policies.summary: The current CBC visitor table expressly labels these named ordinary-passport nationalities ‘Visa Required Unless Exempted’. The portal documents an online pre-travel application but does not directly establish electronic visa issuance, so this remains advance visa required rather than eVisa.
conditions: Visitor visa must be applied for before travel; the official page describes an online application, but does not state that the issued visa is electronic.
The table’s work, residence, re-entry permit, US/Canada/UK resident and specified third-country-visa waivers are conditional and are not normalized.
Admission, duration, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service and special-document rules remain separate.

policies.title: United Arab Emirates citizenship
policies.summary: A UAE ordinary passport belongs to a UAE citizen and is outside the foreign visitor-visa schedule.
conditions: Does not decide a dual national’s document choice, residence, departure, work, military-service, or case-specific border treatment.

policies.title: GCC citizens: visa-free entry
policies.summary: UAE Government guidance expressly says GCC citizens do not need a visa to enter the UAE.
conditions: The traveller must produce a GCC-country passport or national ID card at entry. This is a citizen rule, not a GCC-resident rule.
The separate GCC-resident electronic visa applies to qualifying residents and companions and does not alter this GCC-citizen exemption.
The reviewed sources do not establish work, residence, transit requiring entry, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: MOFA schedule: named visa-free ordinary passport entries
policies.summary: The current MOFA non-citizen schedule marks these named nationality entries Visa Free.
conditions: This maps the schedule country/passport entries only. It does not establish a common duration, entry count, extension, employment right, residence right, or special-document rule.
UAE Government guidance says passports must be valid for at least six months from entry and that arrival eligibility may change; admission remains subject to border and security decisions.

Hong Kong is limited to the schedule named Hong Kong SAR entry; it does not establish PRC, Macao, Taiwan, travel-document, British National (Overseas), or another special passport treatment. Kosovo and Vatican likewise represent only their named ordinary-country entries.
Do not re-label an optional sponsor, airline, hotel, agency, residence-conditioned, transit, or other purpose-specific route as the nationality-wide default.

policies.title: MOFA named ordinary passports: advance electronic tourist visa
policies.summary: MOFA marks these nationalities Visa Required rather than Visa Free. The UAE’s all-nationalities self-sponsored five-year tourist visa is applied for and issued electronically, so the nationality-wide least-onerous advance route is normalized as evisa.
conditions: MOFA's Visa Required label establishes that no visa-free nationality default applies. UAE Government guidance makes a self-sponsored five-year tourist visa available to all nationalities, and ICP states that the visa is received by email and downloadable electronically; this supports evisa, not visa_on_arrival or traditional visa_required, under the project taxonomy.

The five-year route has material eligibility conditions, including the stated funds, UAE-valid health insurance and onward/return ticket. Approval and border admission remain discretionary; it does not establish a no-document or no-fee route.

The ICP 25 June 2026 announcement creates a separate residence-conditioned 14- or 60-day entry-visa option for India, Indonesia, Viet Nam, Thailand, the Philippines, Kenya, and South Africa. It does not replace the nationality-wide electronic tourist-visa route.

For that conditional route, the qualifying residence permit must be from the US, an EU Member State, UK, Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand or Canada; accompanying family members must meet the stated nationality and relationship conditions.
No conclusion is drawn about residence, work, study, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, travel-document, or other special-document routes.

application.label: ICP Issuance of a Visa
steps: Select the suitable tourism/visit visa category on ICP Smart Services or the ICP Smart App.
Submit the application, required passport and supporting documents, and pay the applicable fees.
After approval, download the electronically issued visa received by email and carry the required supporting documents for border inspection.

policies.title: Uruguay: named ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: The Ministry of Interior’s current common-passport schedule expressly marks these passport issuers as not needing a visa for temporary admission. This is a visa-free baseline, not an eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The schedule is limited to the ordinary/common-passport column. Passport type, purpose, activity and duration footnotes remain applicable.

For South Korea, Dominica, Guyana, Latvia, Russia and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, the no-visa treatment is tourist-only or subject to prior consultation for work or stays beyond the stated period; this candidate records only the short visitor baseline.

Malaysia has 30-day temporary admission without a visa. Hong Kong is covered only for passports marked HKSAR, which directly matches the catalog’s HKSAR passport. Macao is expressly exempt for its common passport and travel document.

No eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is identified by the cited nationality schedule. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, third-country-document and final-admission cases are excluded.

policies.title: Uruguay: named and explicit-residual ordinary passports require advance visa
policies.summary: The current Ministry of Interior schedule expressly marks these ordinary passports as needing a visa or, for passport issuers not in its named exemption list, applies its explicit rule that the remaining countries need a visa. The normalized baseline is visa_required: the official process is consular and advance, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The schedule footnote says these marked (5) require prior authorization. The policy remains visa_required whether the authority labels the advance route as prior authorization or consular visa.

Palestine’s ordinary-passport row says admission is granted with prior consultation; the Foreign Ministry’s current prior-consultation process is a consular visa process, so it is likewise normalized as visa_required.

The Foreign Ministry says a tourist-visa applicant must request a consular interview in advance; after authorization the visa is stamped in the passport. An appointment, form, document upload or processing inquiry is not an eVisa.
Taiwan’s row says a travel certificate has been required since 5 December 2018; this does not establish a visa-free, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.

The schedule lists conditional visa exemptions for specified Dominican and PRC passport holders with valid third-country visas and port restrictions. Those conditional third-country-document routes are excluded and do not alter this nationality-only baseline.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, special-document and final-admission cases are excluded.

policies.title: American Samoa: named Entry Permit Waiver Program passports
policies.summary: The current American Samoa Administrative Code names these citizenships for a 30-day Entry Permit Waiver Program route, but requires prior approved OK-to-Board authorization.
conditions: The traveler must obtain the territorial OK-to-Board authorization at least three business days before travel; the waiver is therefore normalized as ETA, not visa-free.
The program permits tourism and specified business only for up to 30 days; it requires a machine-readable passport, onward travel, lodging/host confirmation, fee, and admissibility.
Citizenship by investment is excluded. Work, credit study, residence, commercial-vessel boarding, diplomatic/official, special-document and other routes are excluded.
The Attorney General may modify the list by memorandum; entry remains discretionary.

application.label: American Samoa visitor-permit portal
steps: Apply for the territorial visitor/waiver processing route before travel.
Provide the required travel, lodging and onward-travel information and pay the fee.
Present the approved OK-to-Board document to Immigration on arrival.

policies.title: American Samoa: Qatar U.S.-visa-waiver 30-day visitor permit
policies.summary: The current American Samoa Government waiver-country list names Qatar, and its current visitor portal requires a pre-travel, emailed 30-day permit for U.S.-visa-waiver-country travelers.
conditions: The traveler must apply before arrival, receive the emailed permit, and present it to Immigration; the pre-travel electronic approval is normalized as ETA rather than visa-free.
The current route is limited to a 30-day visitor permit and remains subject to passport validity, fee, purpose, admissibility, entry and other territorial conditions.
Work, residence, credit study, transit, diplomatic/official, special-document, U.S.-visa-holder and individual-admission routes are excluded.

application.label: American Samoa U.S. Visa / Waiver 30-Day Visitor Permit
steps: Apply and pay before travel using the territorial visitor-permit workflow.
Receive the emailed permit before departure.
Present the permit to American Samoa Immigration on arrival.

policies.title: Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands: Visa Waiver Program ESTA
policies.summary: CBP confirms that VWP-country citizens traveling for short business or tourism to Puerto Rico or the U.S. Virgin Islands require approved ESTA.
conditions: Only tourism or business stays of 90 days or less under the federal VWP are covered; ESTA must be approved before travel.
A compliant e-passport is required. Current federal disqualifications include specified prior travel/presence and certain dual nationalities; an approved ESTA does not guarantee admission.
